papers.title: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Autonomous Vehicle Overtaking with Bezier Curve Path
papers.abstract: Rapid advancements in autonomous vehicle technology have significantly improved driving safety, yet formulating safe and efficient overtaking strategies remains a key challenge. This study proposes an algorithmic framework for autonomous vehicles to perform overtaking maneuvers, validated through comprehensive simulations. The framework utilizes Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) to manage complex vehicle dynamics, processing real-time velocity and steering angle inputs. Real-time feedback from LiDAR sensors enables dynamic trajectory generation using Bezier curve formulations, which provide reference inputs for the pure pursuit algorithm to guide the NMPC during overtaking. Once the vehicle aligns with the obstacle, the Bezier curve is adjusted to smoothly return the vehicle to its original path. The approach was thoroughly evaluated using the Robot Operating System (ROS) and Gazebo, ensuring realistic visualization and robust performance under dynamic conditions.
papers.venue: JAREE (Journal on Advanced Research in Electrical Engineering)

papers.title: Agentic World Action Models
papers.abstract: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands. Code serves two complementary roles: it structures multi-step prediction and control within the world model and represents skills as reusable programs for subsequent agentic execution. We further introduce an automated curation pipeline that labels robot and human video trajectories with aligned programs and consolidates recurring routines into reusable skill libraries. Evaluations on RoboTwin 2.0 and physical bimanual manipulation tasks show improved task performance over VLA and WAM baselines, alongside gains in language following, semantic reasoning and robustness, demonstrating that agentic code enables connection between planning, prediction and execution within WAMs.

papers.title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models
papers.abstract: Video world models predict future frames from past frames and actions. They serve as simulators in which agents train, plan or are evaluated, and that humans can control interactively. They generate in the latent space of a video autoencoder, whose compression sets their cost per frame and how long each action waits to take effect. Yet world models often reuse the autoencoders of text-to-video generators, built for offline generation with no agent waiting and, without their training data and code, not retrainable at another compression. We therefore ask how, where and how much a world model should compress. We build CADRE, an open family of causal diffusion representation autoencoders spanning multiple spatio-temporal compressions. Its members differ only in a small bottleneck on frozen features and share a diffusion decoder self-distilled to one or a few steps. We train the same world model on each autoencoder in two domains, manipulation and navigation, with two environments each. CADRE forms most of the latency-quality frontier, especially with a moving camera. Our study also leads to four findings. At strong compression, a diffusion decoder is sharper than perceptual regression. In robot manipulation, temporal compression is more effective in the autoencoder than in the world model. Manipulation and navigation call for opposite compressions: temporal compression costs little when the camera is still, and spatial compression when it moves. Surprisingly, with a still camera, coarser spatial tokens hurt motion far more than image quality. Code, models and a live demo are at https://kyutai.org/blog/2026-10-21-cadre

papers.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
papers.abstract: Sequential decision-making under partial observability is difficult because agents must explore to infer hidden, task-relevant information before acting effectively. Learning such information-gathering behaviors tabula rasa via online reinforcement learning is sample-inefficient, whereas offline imitation averages expert actions across hidden states and fails to learn exploration. In this work, we propose ASTEROID, a simple and effective student--teacher supervised learning framework that can learn test-time exploration. Although a privileged expert never needs to explore, we demonstrate that a history-conditioned student can learn to do so when trained with on-policy contexts: the student first collects on-policy context under partial observability, and the privileged expert provides action labels conditioned on that context. By distilling expert actions directly conditioned on the student's on-policy history, the student learns to systematically resolve partial observability, i.e., search while uncertain and exploit once the hidden state is revealed. This enables efficient test-time exploration (similar to Bayesian posterior sampling) without incurring the impractical training-data costs of reinforcement learning. Across a diverse range of eleven different environments, including discrete exploration benchmarks, robotic manipulation, navigation, and Procgen environments, ASTEROID achieves ~2x higher returns under fixed exploration budgets, uses ~100x fewer interactions than RL baselines, and outperforms frontier models at exploration. Finally, our method transfers policies trained in simulation to vision-denied real-world robot manipulation, exhibiting efficient exploration and increasing success by +40% over standard distillation. Overall, it provides a simple yet surprisingly effective framework to learn efficient test-time exploration.

papers.title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise in robotic manipulation, but imitation learning (IL) alone often struggles to master complex long-horizon skills. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers an effective avenue for further improving VLA policies. However, existing VLA-RL methods typically suffer from delayed and biased credit assignment due to trajectory-level sparse rewards, while imbalanced subtask mastery creates bottlenecks that limit overall performance. To address these challenges, we propose AtomicRL, an RL post-training framework that leverages atomic task structures for reliable credit assignment and adaptive exploration. AtomicRL introduces Semantic-Aware Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses semantic-aware gating to constrain TD residuals from failed atomic subtasks from propagating across task boundaries, mitigating credit contamination while preserving intra-subtask credit assignment and value bootstrapping. In addition, Bottleneck-Adaptive Target Exploration (BATE) dynamically coordinates task sampling and local exploration incentives based on the mastery of individual atomic subtasks, directing learning toward the remaining bottlenecks. Finally, we develop a Real2Sim2Real pipeline that bridges online RL in simulation with real-world deployment, facilitating practical transfer to physical robots. On LIBERO-LONG, AtomicRL achieves absolute performance gains of 3.6% and 4.0% over PPO across two VLA architectures. On CALVIN ABC-D, it improves full-task performance by up to 9.5% over PPO. Combined with the Real2Sim2Real pipeline, AtomicRL further improves real-world task performance by an average of 21.3%. These results demonstrate that AtomicRL effectively improves the learning efficiency and manipulation performance of VLA policies on long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: Object- and Task-Aware Active Perception for Safe Navigation of Mobile Manipulators in Semi-Static Environments
papers.abstract: Mobile manipulators must navigate safely in cluttered, partially unknown environments across logistics, manufacturing, and service applications. Semi-static changes between robot visits can lead to outdated scene knowledge and increased collision risk. We propose an active perception framework that enables a high degree-of-freedom (DoF) mobile manipulator to inspect uncertain or safety-critical regions with its hand camera during navigation. A probabilistic, object- and task-aware next-best-view (NBV) formulation prioritizes observations near the desired path and around uncertain or potentially changing objects. The perception objective is integrated into hierarchical-task model predictive control (HTMPC), exploiting kinematic redundancy for viewpoint adjustment while preserving the higher priority of base-trajectory tracking. The system unifies navigation, map maintenance, and active perception in a closed loop. Real-world tests show improved map consistency, reduced task-dependent map entropy, and lower navigation risk than passive or non-task-aware baselines. Additional simulation and real-world sequences demonstrate responses to controlled semi-static scene changes.

papers.title: A PDE-theory-guided neural operator and the long-time relaxation of the two-dimensional anisotropic Boussinesq system
papers.abstract: We design a neural operator for the two-dimensional Boussinesq system with anisotropic dissipation on the periodic box, guided by a rigorous analysis of its long-time behavior. The operator maps a small perturbation of hydrostatic equilibrium, of amplitude $\varepsilon$, to the vorticity at a late time. We prove that the flow relaxes to a stratified shear flow, with the horizontally averaged vorticity staying within $O(\varepsilon^2)$ of its initial value $\barω_0$ and the oscillation about it of order $\varepsilon$. Accordingly, the network outputs $\barω_0$ plus these two parts, each scaled to its size, which grows as $\varepsilon^2$ and $\varepsilon$, respectively. Without this guidance the training either does not converge or misses the $\varepsilon^2$ growth. With it, one network reproduces, sample by sample on $2\times10^3$ test runs over a factor of $23$ in amplitude, the quantity bounded by the theorem to a median error of $2.2$ percent. Being fast and differentiable with respect to the initial data, the network is also used to search the space of initial data, and with every candidate checked by the solver the search finds initial data for which this quantity is $4.4$ times the largest value among the test runs, raising the lower bound for the constant of the theorem by that factor.

papers.title: RangeNav: Task-Aligned LiDAR Range-Image Pretraining for Robot Navigation
papers.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots operating in dense crowds and cluttered sites require $360^\circ$ perception to react to surrounding hazards. While panoramic LiDAR offers full-surround coverage, learning representations within reinforcement learning (RL) is sample-inefficient under sparse rewards, and existing 3D pretrained point-cloud encoders are too memory-heavy for massively parallel RL simulation. We present RangeNav, a compact (183k parameters) LiDAR range-image encoder pretrained entirely on synthetic data. RangeNav uses anisotropic convolutions and circular padding to handle the extreme aspect ratio and azimuthal seam of range images. We pretrain the network using a navigation-aligned objective combining range reconstruction, semantic segmentation, and bird's-eye-view (BEV) prediction, then freeze it for policy learning. In simulation, adding semantic and BEV supervision increases success rates over a reconstruction-only baseline by an average of 32.03 and 23.73 percentage points (pp) in procedurally generated training and out-of-distribution realistic test environments, respectively. Zero-shot real-world deployments on a Unitree B2-W quadruped demonstrate robust navigation through dense crowds, low-light settings, and construction zones where limited-field-of-view depth policies struggle. Code and models will be open-sourced.

papers.title: Post-hoc Epistemic Uncertainty for Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies need to recognize gaps in their training knowledge to request useful demonstrations or assistance in new situations, especially when failures are costly. Disagreement within an ensemble of independently trained policies can guide these decisions, but requires training and running multiple policies. We propose post-hoc kernel-variance heads that estimate epistemic uncertainty from the embeddings of a single policy. Each head computes the conditional variance of a Gaussian process conditioned on embeddings from the training demonstrations. Fitting requires no regression targets or gradient updates and leaves the policy unchanged. In experiments with SmolVLA on LIBERO-10, the kernel variance heads perform competitively with two-policy ensemble scores in task-level correlation with task success, in demonstration acquisition during active learning, and in referral to a stronger supervisor policy as a proxy for human assistance. For SmolVLA, the head on the vision-language backbone reduces uncertainty-scoring time by up to approximately a factor of 50 compared with ensemble scores, while also substantially reducing setup costs. We also show that the established evaluation protocol on LIBERO-10 primarily rewards recognition of coverage differences between tasks, while execution variability weakens assessment of within-task rankings. Thus, controlled perturbations provide a complementary evaluation: modality-specific heads identify unfamiliar camera, instruction, or state inputs, while fused heads can detect unfamiliar combinations of individually familiar inputs. With a supervisor proxy trained on the evaluated perturbation families, the decoder head improves within-task referral over ensemble disagreement. These findings show that useful uncertainty estimates for adaptive robot learning can be obtained from a single policy.

papers.title: Model Predictive Control: Systematic Design Tailored to Nonholonomic Systems
papers.abstract: Nonholonomic systems are ubiquitous in applications such as transportation and robotics, yet their control remains challenging. In order to achieve asymptotic stability of a desired equilibrium, model predictive control (MPC) schemes without stabilizing terminal conditions have recently been proposed for nonholonomic kinematic systems. However, this approach still required lengthy system-specific calculations. This paper eliminates the need for these auxiliary calculations, as we propose a streamlined systematic design for MPC stage costs tailored to nonholonomic systems, utilizing the concepts of privileged coordinates and nonholonomic weights. Furthermore, the proposed design methodology is extended beyond purely kinematic models to a wider class of systems with non-negligible dynamics, and we highlight the geometric meaning of the resulting MPC stage costs. The systematic procedure is demonstrated using an articulated vehicle as an example.

papers.title: DriveMLP: When Training Strategy Outperforms Model Complexity in Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Learning motion planning policies that remain reliable under closed-loop execution is a central challenge in Autonomous Driving (AD). Imitation Learning (IL) scales well to large AD datasets but suffers from distribution shift, causal confusion, and compounding errors under closed-loop execution. In contrast, Reinforcement Learning (RL) typically requires handcrafted rule-based rewards and massive simulation. We study a simple closed-loop IL framework that uses RL purely as an optimization tool, guided by a trajectory-distance reward derived from logged expert data. We refer to this training strategy as Expert-Guided RL (EGRL). Through a controlled empirical study we find evidence that the training procedure, rather than model size and complexity, accounts for a substantial part of the performance gains. We then introduce DriveMLP, a lightweight MLP policy trained with EGRL, as a simple instantiation of these findings. It achieves a score of 86.51 on the nuPlan Val14 Reactive benchmark, a +3.2 point improvement over the previous best IL planner (Flow Planner), with >15x faster inference. Code is available at: https://github.com/alessandro-canevaro/DriveMLP .

papers.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning for Short-Term Atmospheric Seeing Forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate short-term forecasting of atmospheric seeing is of significant interest for astronomical observations and free-space optical communication systems, where rapid variations in optical turbulence can affect system performance and operational planning. In this work, we benchmark machine learning models for predicting atmospheric seeing up to two hours in advance, with a particular focus on probabilistic forecasting and uncertainty quantification. We compare two probabilistic approaches, Gaussian Processes (GPs) and a normalizing-flow- based model (FloTS), against deterministic recurrent neural network (RNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) baselines. All models are trained and evaluated on seeing measurements from the Maunakea summit. We assess the models using both deterministic metrics, including the root mean square error and the Pearson correlation coefficient, and probabilistic metrics that evaluate the quality and calibration of predictive uncertainty estimates. The results show that deep learning approaches outperform standard recurrent networks for short-term forecasting, with LSTM and FloTS achieving the best overall predictive accuracy. While Gaussian Processes provide a useful probabilistic baseline, their predictive distributions are limited by the Gaussian assumption. FloTS combines competitive forecasting accuracy with flexible uncertainty quantification and produces the most informative probabilistic forecasts.

papers.title: End-to-End Reinforcement Learning for Quadrupedal Jumping in Lunar Gravity
papers.abstract: Legged robots can extend planetary exploration to rugged and discontinuous terrain that is inaccessible to conventional rovers. In lunar gravity, jumping further expands this mobility by enabling robots to cross obstacles and gaps that cannot be traversed by walking alone. We present a multistage reinforcement-learning approach that produces a single end-to-end control policy for commanded point-to-point jumping under lunar gravity. The resulting policy has a simple architecture and relies exclusively on mission-compatible onboard sensing, making its deployment on a real lunar mission plausible. In simulation, the learned policy performs accurate point-to-point jumps with landing errors smaller than the robot's body size. We analyze the torque and power demands of lunar jumping and characterize performance degradation under extreme outlier events, including control-update freezes of up to \SI{1}{s} during flight. Hardware transfer demonstrates that the policy can successfully execute a vertical jump under lunar-gravity offloading. Furthermore, the measured torque and power profiles are consistent with the simulation results and remain within the robot's hardware limits.

papers.title: Fast Bayesian Optimization Through Linear Models
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is typically used only for problems where the underlying function is deemed "expensive" (e.g. in time or money), with the speed of the BO algorithm being of little importance. In the real world, however, problems span a continuous range of values, going from cheap to expensive. In this paper, we present BO algorithms through the lens of a speed-performance Pareto frontier: we compare BO against faster algorithms like CMA-ES, and highlight how certain regions of the Pareto frontier are currently empty. As a solution, we propose a new set of fast BO methods that exploit the linear structure in existing BO algorithms, for both continuous and combinatorial inputs (from ~10 to 6000+ dimensions). Our methods achieve performance similar to state-of-the-art BO, while being more than $10^2\times$ to $10^3\times$ faster, opening the field of BO to an entirely new class of problems.

papers.title: Certified Neural Approximation of Robust Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Model predictive control is a high-performance control method, but it incurs comparatively high online computational costs across many control tasks and is challenging to realize in low-level hardware settings. To address this, we present a framework for generating neural network controllers that provably inherit the safety and stability guarantees of a robust model predictive policy. In contrast to approaches based on post-verification or additional online safety filters, our method provides constructive, a priori design conditions that ensure preservation of recursive feasibility and stability before deployment. We treat the approximation error as a bounded input disturbance, which is addressed in the MPC design. This allows the neural network controller to directly inherit robustness from the underlying model predictive controller, which enables the transfer of guarantees to the approximation. The design process is an offline, constructive synthesis pipeline and can be implemented once Lipschitz bounds are specified. We further demonstrate in simulation that the learned controller reproduces the closed-loop behavior of the original controller while reducing online computation.

papers.title: Distance Field Driven Reinforcement Learning for Reactive and Robust Collision Avoidance
papers.abstract: Robust and reactive collision avoidance remains a central challenge for deploying Reinforcement Learning (RL) policies on real robotic manipulators, particularly when transferring behaviours learned in simulation to the physical world. This paper presents an RL framework that integrates the Euclidean Distance Field (EDF) directly into the observation space, providing the agent with continuous geometric cues that support stable and responsive avoidance behaviours. By leveraging the rich spatial information encoded in the EDF, the method enables a streamlined reward formulation that achieves effective obstacle avoidance both with and without Artificial Potential Field guidance. The proposed approach is validated on a 7-DoF redundant manipulator, demonstrating zero-shot transfer from simulation to real hardware. Despite being trained exclusively with randomised static objects, the deployed policy generalizes to previously unseen real environments and exhibits robust online avoidance of dynamic obstacles. These results highlight the potential of EDF-based representations to mitigate the sim-to-real gap and support reliable and real-time collision-aware behaviour in complex and changing environments.

papers.title: One Act, Many Masks: Effect-Marginal Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Recent advances in multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) have substantially improved the performance of LLM agents on complex, long-horizon interactive tasks. However, despite progress in fine-grained credit assignment, policy optimization still applies these learning signals through response-specific probability ratios. Different textual responses can induce the same executable effect, yet credit differences arising from subsequent outcomes remain tied to their individual textual realizations. We identify this mismatch as credit-update misalignment. Our analysis reveals that credit-text pairing directly shapes policy-update directions, even when the policy context and executable effect are held fixed. Motivated by this finding, we propose Effect-Marginal Policy Optimization (EMPO), which aligns policy optimization with execution-level equivalence through an effect-level surrogate that couples updates across alternative textual realizations. EMPO preserves the original credit signals, integrates with both trajectory-level and step-level credit estimators, and requires no additional critics or rollouts. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and Sokoban show that EMPO outperforms strong baselines in both task performance and learning efficiency.

papers.title: BIRD-RL: Scaling Agentic Reinforcement Learning over Stateful Data-Centric Environments
papers.abstract: While agentic reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for training small language models (SLMs), existing frameworks are predominantly tool-centric and struggle with data-centric environments. Specifically, applying tool-centric frameworks to stateful tasks like SQL debugging introduces severe spatial inefficiencies since proper environment isolation typically requires a separate database container per rollout. Naively reusing databases without tracking evolving states across multi-turn interactions causes trajectory contamination and cross-trajectory interference, which severely destabilizes policy updates. To overcome these bottlenecks, we introduce BIRD-RL, a novel four-stage agentic RL curriculum that alternately enhances foundational agent reasoning and trajectory-adaptive on-policy exploration to circumvent the instability inherently associated with direct end-to-end learning. Crucially, to support this curriculum, BIRD-RL is driven by a Trajectory-scoped Persistent Execution Infrastructure, which enables safe database replica reuse while preserving trajectory isolation. This design improves spatial RL efficiency by 12.8x, successfully enabling scalable agentic RL for complex data-centric tasks without needs of Kubernettes. Empirical evaluations on the BIRD-CRITIC-SQLite benchmark demonstrate that our 7B and 14B models achieve Success Rates of 44.40% and 48.00%, respectively, showing competitive performance against strong proprietary model-based agents such as Claude-Opus-4.6 Agent (48.20%). Furthermore, BIRD-RL successfully trains unified SLMs capable of both advanced SQL debugging and generation, highlighting its broader potential for multi-objective optimization across heterogeneous, real-world data-centric tasks.

papers.title: Alternative Strategies for Active Learning with Bayesian Bradley Terry Model
papers.abstract: Comparative judgement uses pairwise comparisons to rank items, but recovering accurate rankings from a limited number of judgements depends on both the inference method and the pairs selected. We developed a Bayesian Bradley-Terry model (BBTM) that uses Polya-Gamma data augmentation for efficient Gibbs sampling and quantifies uncertainty in latent abilities and ranks. We propose three active learning strategies based on the knowledge gradient (KG) principle. We define our acquisition functions using Kendall's tau distance, posterior rank entropy, and posterior separation. Approximate one-step updates to posterior moments reduce the computational cost of evaluating candidate pairs. We also introduce Posterior Separation Reliability (PSR), which measures the spread of posterior mean abilities relative to posterior uncertainty. It provides an internal indicator of ranking reliability without requiring a reference ranking. In synthetic experiments covering different item counts, comparison budgets, and noise levels, BBTM generally recovers ranking more accurately than preference-based Bayesian comparative judgement (PBCJ). At low to moderate noise levels, the pairwise entropy pair selection strategy performs best in ranking recovery. However, at the highest noise levels, the KG strategy based on posterior separation produces better point rankings. PSR increases alongside improvements in ranking accuracy as comparisons accumulate. Robustness experiments identify the proportion of informative outcomes needed to meet specified accuracy targets within a fixed comparison budget. In a moderate noise setting, replacing 30\% of outcomes with random choices has little effect on ranking performance. These findings demonstrate the value of Bayesian inference and active learning pair selection for recovering ranks from limited, noisy paired comparisons.

papers.title: Integrating Flow Matching and Model Predictive Control for Safe Robot Navigation
papers.abstract: Learning-based path planners based on diffusion and flow matching can generate diverse trajectories from demonstrations but typically lack mechanisms for constraint satisfaction and collision avoidance during deployment. This work proposes a framework that combines flow-matching-based path planning with model predictive path-following control to integrate data-driven path generation with real-time, constraint-aware execution. The flow-matching model captures multimodal path distributions, while the predictive controller adapts motion online to satisfy state and input constraints and avoid obstacles using updated local sensor information. An event-triggered re-planning scheme incorporates predictive control solutions into subsequent path generation, promoting collision-free navigation in environments with previously unseen obstacles. Simulation results for mobile robot navigation demonstrate robust performance across cluttered environments. The framework provides a systematic approach to combining flow matching with predictive control for adaptive, data-driven navigation.

papers.title: LLM-Based Exogenous World Modeling for Dynamic Scheduling
papers.abstract: Dynamic scheduling requires dispatching online arrivals while anticipating future jobs, as poor decisions can compound downstream costs under nonlinear tardiness objectives. We show that a pretrained large language model (LLM) can serve as the exogenous component of a structured world model, forecasting uncertain future job arrivals. Specifically, we exploit an afterstate decomposition, which separates known deterministic shop transitions from uncertain exogenous job arrivals, enabling the LLM to forecast only the latter through a compact belief representation. Building on this, we develop Afterstate World-Model Planning (AWMP), which combines an evolved, belief-conditioned dispatching strategy with short scenario-based rollouts. A surprise-triggered refresh mechanism queries the LLM only when newly observed arrivals deviate sufficiently from previous forecast, and online residual self-calibration further conditions the LLM on its recent forecast errors to handle nonstationary arrivals. Across diverse arrival distributions, AWMP reduces weighted tardiness by 6-21% on dynamic job-shop and 22-46% on flexible job-shop benchmarks, relative to the best of eight classical priority-dispatching rules.

papers.title: Design and Tuning of Multi-Agent Systems Using Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization
papers.abstract: Designing effective multi-agent systems (MAS) remains a challenging and resource-intensive task. We propose a Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization framework for automatically discovering task-specific MAS topologies. The approach combines evolutionary operators to generate diverse workflow graphs with Bayesian optimization to focus cost intensive evaluations on promising candidates. In contrast to LLM-based candidate selection, our approach uses a graph-aware Gaussian Process and Expected Improvement to provide an explicit selection criterion during evolutionary search. We evaluate the method on BigCodeBench for code generation and on a tabular preprocessing benchmark using TabPFN. On BigCodeBench, evolved architectures achieve the highest overall performance among the evaluated agent systems. On temporal tabular datasets, optimized MAS preprocessing improves over the default TabPFN model on several tasks, while remaining competitive on IID datasets. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of Bayesian selection for guiding evolutionary MAS search under expensive evaluation budgets.

papers.title: A Decade of Learning-Based Control: From Theoretic Foundations to Practical Deployment
papers.abstract: Motivated by ten years of Learning-Based Control Invited Sessions at the IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC), this tutorial paper reviews key advances at the intersection of machine learning and control. We focus on methods that combine the flexibility of machine learning techniques with the structure and theoretical foundations of control to design autonomous systems that are capable, reliable, and safe. We first introduce core notions for establishing stability and safety guarantees, then review approaches that learn dynamics models to improve control under uncertainty, and finally discuss data-driven methods that directly synthesize or learn policies, including reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and Bayesian optimization. We further discuss representative applications and open challenges. The goal is to provide an accessible entry point to the field and to support continued progress toward reliable learning-based control in real-world systems. To support learning and practical exploration, we share implementations and illustrative examples along with our discussion, together with additional resources on our website: https://learning-based-control.github.io/tutorial/.

papers.title: How Representational Priors Shape Generalization in World Action Models
papers.abstract: World action models (WAMs) are shown to substantially diverge under generalization performance based on their generative backbones. We investigate this gap through the representational geometry that WAMs inherit from their backbones and how policy training reorganizes it. Our central hypothesis is that a useful representational prior would structure geometry that separates nuisance information from the in-distribution manifold in advance of training as a policy. We quantify this with nuisance orthogonality; orthogonality of the feature under visual variation outside the empirical in-distribution manifold. Across various image and video backbones, we show that a higher orthogonality from the representational prior is associated with stronger robustness to visual variations after WAM training, enabling policy generalization measurable prospectively for world models. In addition, analyzing the resulting robust WAMs reveals nuisance suppression; relative suppression of feature displacement caused by such variations and robust action generation of the policy. Together, these findings provide a geometric perspective on how the representational prior of the world model shapes the generalization performance of WAMs.

papers.title: State-Dependent Objective Coordination for End-to-End Balance and Navigation
papers.abstract: Traditional robotic navigation systems separate mapping, planning, and low-level control through cascaded modules, introducing computational overhead and accumulated latency. End-to-end reinforcement learning offers a compact unified policy that maps onboard observations directly to control actions. However, on inherently unstable platforms such as two-wheeled inverted-pendulum robots, navigation progress and obstacle avoidance can conflict with attitude stabilization in a strongly state-dependent manner. We propose a lightweight state-dependent objective coordination method for integrated navigation and control. A pitch-conditioned scalarization coefficient $β(s)\in[0,1]$ adjusts the relative contributions of balance stabilization and navigation objectives during training, without extra control hierarchies or auxiliary attitude-stabilization controllers, such as proportional-integral-derivative (PID) or linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) controllers. To support zero-shot deployment, simulation training models execution delay, action hold, asynchronous and noisy observations, and dynamics uncertainty. Gradient analysis reveals persistent directional interference and state-dependent variation in the objectives' relative scales. Comparisons with alternative reward-weighting, constraint, training, and control-structure strategies show that PPO+$β(s)$, where PPO denotes proximal policy optimization, achieves 98% and 95% success rates with small attitude excursions on the fixed obstacle map and the randomly generated high-obstacle-density map, respectively. Zero-shot hardware experiments further demonstrate bounded attitude behavior and consistent obstacle avoidance using only onboard observations. Training and evaluation code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

papers.title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
papers.abstract: Frontier black-box Large Language Model (LLM) agents are proficient at long-horizon reasoning and precise action generation. However, when it comes to a specific agentic task, they have no internalized knowledge of how that particular environment unfolds. A world model offers a natural remedy, providing the agent with environment specific knowledge by foreseeing how the environment will respond to the action it is about to take. Prior world models for LLM agents mainly predict next observations at each step, which is costly and often uninformative because individual observations provide limited task-relevant guidance and not every step requires call for foresight. This raises a key question: what a world model should predict and when should it be invoked for agentic tasks? Our pilot study suggests that world model guidance is most useful when it anticipates pitfalls within a bounded multi-step future. Motivated by this, we introduce Pitfall Anticipation World Model (PAWM), which selectively intervenes when a potential pitfall arises and predicts the impending failure to steer the agent away from it. PAWM is trained in two stages: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on synthetic data labeled with agent pitfalls, followed by GRPO co-training with a black-box LLM to further optimize it in the target environment. PAWM improves Claude Sonnet 4.5 performance by 24.3% on ScienceWorld and 7.7% on WebArena-Lite, outperforming a range of baselines. These results demonstrate that PAWM provides an effective form of world model guidance for black-box LLM agents.

papers.title: Causal world models under physical parameter shifts
papers.abstract: World models predict how embodied systems evolve under actions, but their accuracy can degrade when physical conditions move outside the training distribution. We study two components of causal modeling: which inputs a predictor may use, and how its mechanism computes their effects. In a synthetic benchmark with shortcut features, a frozen dependency mask derived from paired interventions reduces mean out-of-distribution (OOD) RMSE from 1.769 for a fully connected predictor to 0.697, close to the generator-oracle mask (0.694). For robot link-mass extrapolation in CausalWorld, with disjoint training and test mass ranges, we develop finger-local world models in which link masses enter inertia and dynamics-bias terms through explicit affine coefficients, actions act through either a learned torque network or the known PD controller, and learned residuals capture contact-related effects. Compared with a separately trained control whose mass inputs are fixed at training means, the known-PD model turns out-of-range masses into a consistent predictive gain: median time-averaged joint R2 over 150-step rollouts rises from 0.609 to 0.727, with improvement in all ten task-seed runs (exact two-sided sign test, p = 0.002). In a shared 100-step forecast, the learned-torque model is competitive with the strongest recurrent robotic world model (RWM) configuration (median joint R2 of 0.755 - 0.768 versus 0.752), whereas supplying out-of-range masses sharply degrades the MLP and recurrent predictors. These results indicate that how a physical parameter enters the dynamics mechanism determines whether its out-of-range value helps or harms prediction.

papers.title: Verification of a Conjugate Heat Transfer Model in OpenFOAM for a Simplified Medical Device Geometry
papers.abstract: Article submitted to the Journal of Verification, Validation and Uncertainty Quantification.AbstractComputational models and simulations (CM&S) are increasingly used in medical device development, yet their adoption in regulatory decision-making remains limited due to challenges in establishing model credibility. This study presents a structured and reproducible verification framework for a computational model of a simplified medical device involving conjugate heat transfer using OpenFOAM's chtMultiRegionFoam solver. Code verification is performed using analytical benchmarks for laminar pipe flow, radial heat conduction, and transient thermal diffusion yielding observed orders of convergence of p=1.95, p=2.08, and p=2.15 (at 0.025 s) respectively. Solution verification evaluates discretization error through systematic mesh and time step refinement and regression-based extrapolation using the StREEQ method. Results show that spatial and temporal discretization errors in transient coupled simulations interact and cannot be assessed independently. Co-refinement is required to capture true convergence behavior, while independent refinement yields polluted convergence rates. Computational cost analysis demonstrates diminishing returns with refinement and highlights that runtime does not vary monotonically with discretization parameters due to solver convergence behavior. The use of a simplified geometry enables rigorous verification while retaining the dominant physics of the system. Grounded in a risk-informed framework consistent with ASME V&V 40 Standard, this study demonstrates that a level of verification rigor beyond minimal practice can be achieved through targeted model simplification and systematic analysis under realistic computational constraints. All simulation inputs and analysis scripts are openly available at https://github.com/plinarodriguez/edds_verification_repo

papers.title: Development of a Modified FDM-Based Bioprinter with Optimized Extrusion Parameters for High-Fidelity Alginate Bioinks and Aortic Valve Scaffold Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Aortic valve disease is a major cause of cardiovascular deaths worldwide. Aortic stenosis increases the workload on the heart and severely alters hemodynamic function by impairing effective blood flow. In recent years, extrusion-based bioprinting technologies have made significant progress in producing patient-specific, biocompatible cardiovascular structures, opening up new opportunities for advanced therapeutic applications. In this study, a commercially available FDM-type 3D printer (ENDER-3 Pro) was mechanically and electronically modified into a fully functional, low-cost bioprinter capable of depositing alginate-gelatin hydrogels with high structural fidelity, despite their low viscosity. The redesigned system integrates a NEMA-17 driven syringe extrusion module equipped with a TR8X8 lead screw, enabling high-resolution pressure-controlled deposition of viscoelastic bioinks. A three-leaflet aortic valve geometry was digitally reconstructed and simplified using Fusion 360 to ensure printability while preserving essential anatomical features. The printing parameters were systematically investigated according to the alginate-based bioinks and set to a nozzle diameter (0.6 mm), layer height (0.6 mm), extrusion multiplier (0.02), and printing speed (5 mm/s). Quantitative shape fidelity assessment, including top-down geometric deviation analysis, confirmed that the bioprinted aortic valve constructs successfully maintained the nominal CAD boundaries. By dynamically optimizing slicing parameters, specifically the extrusion multiplier, rheologically driven deformations such as excessive lateral spreading were effectively mitigated. Although comprehensive evaluation of hemodynamic performance requires future in vitro experiments and coupled fluid–structure interaction (FSI) simulations, the present study establishes a robust and accessible biofabrication framework capable of producing highly complex cardiovascular geometries. Cost-effective and adaptable bioprinting platforms, derived from consumer-grade fused deposition modeling (FDM) systems, can achieve the geometric fidelity and structural stability necessary for advanced cardiovascular tissue engineering. This approach significantly enhances the accessibility of high-precision bioprinting technologies, thereby facilitating broader adoption in both research and translational applications.

papers.title: The impact of long-term aspirin use on patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Due to the aging population and the high incidence of osteoarticular diseases, the demand for the future development of total hip arthroplasty (THA). Aspirin use has increased substantially owing to its multiple benefits. The aim of our study was to explore the influence of Long-Aspirin Use (L-AU) on perioperative complications in patients undergoing THA. By querying the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) database, the data of patients undergoing THA from 2019 to 2022 were acquired after removing irrelevant data. Propensity score matching (PSM) was designed to reduce the impact of demographic and comorbidity characteristics on perioperative complications. T Test , Chi-Square Test, Rank Sum Test, as well as logistic regression analysis, were used for perioperative complications risk analysis and resource consumption analysis. The proportion of ICD-coded long-term aspirin use (L-AU) among patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty in the unweighted NIS analytic sample increased from 12.13% to 18.21% between 2019 and 2022. After multivariable adjustment, L‑AU was significantly associated with elevated risks of any complication, acute myocardial infarction, and acute cerebrovascular disease. Meanwhile, L‑AU was significantly associated with reduced odds of septicemia and respiratory failure, as well as lower odds of prolonged length of stay and lower total hospital costs. No statistically significant associations were observed between L‑AU and most other perioperative complications. In this retrospective analysis, long-term aspirin use was associated with selected in-hospital outcomes among patients undergoing THA, including lower odds of septicemia and respiratory failure and higher odds of acute myocardial infarction and acute cerebrovascular disease. These associations do not establish causality, and the effects of perioperative aspirin continuation, discontinuation, or resumption could not be assessed. Prospective studies with detailed medication and clinical data are needed to clarify the perioperative risks and benefits of aspirin management in this population. This shows that a total of 369,846 patients undergoing primary THA between 2019 and 2022, through exclusion of inappropriate samples among them, obtained the remaining 310,925 patients who were classified into the long-term aspirin use (L-AU) cohort (n=49,613) and matched non-L-AU cohort (n=49,613) after propensity score matching analysis.

papers.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty in Patients with Left Ventricular Assist Devices: Perioperative Management and Clinical Outcome
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) are commonly utilized in severe left-sided heart disease as a bridge to transplantation or long-term treatment. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) improves mobility in these patients but entails numerous perioperative risks. Our study focused on perioperative management and clinical outcomes for LVAD patients undergoing THA, aiming to provide insights into this complex setting. Methods We retrospectively analyzed patients with LVADs who underwent THA at our institution from May 2019 to November 2023. The outcomes of interest were perioperative anticoagulation management, thrombotic or bleeding events, transfusion needs, mortality, surgical site complications, and reoperations. The functional outcome was evaluated using the modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS) and the EQ-5D quality of life score at their last follow-up. Results The cohort consisted of 11 male patients, mean age 68.1 years. Patient survival was recorded over a 22.8-month mean follow-up (range, 1–53). Seven patients (63.6%) required postoperative transfusions and 5/11 patients (45.5%) experienced thromboembolic events. The mean hospital stay after THA was 13.5 days. The overall mortality related-to-disease rate in our series of LVAD patients undergoing primary THA was 27%. Three patients (27.3%) developed surgical site hematomas, which required one additional reoperation, and one of those was infected. Hip functionality improved markedly, with the mean mHHS rising from 27.5 to 72.3. Conclusions THA in LVAD patients is challenging yet feasible, offering significant functional improvements despite the increased perioperative morbidity. Mortality was associated with their underlying disease, but not the surgery.

papers.title: Digital Twin Prototype Framework for Control-Verified Design of Piezoelectric Composite in Adaptive Aerospace Structure
papers.abstract: Abstract This study presents a Digital Twin Prototype (DTP) design framework for a piezoelectric composite curved shell structure, applied to an adaptive aileron trailing-edge control surface. Unlike sequential design approaches, where actuator placement and control feasibility are checked only after the geometry is fixed, the framework integrates SysML requirement capture, finite element analysis, reduced-order modelling (ROM), and constrained Model Predictive Control (MPC) within one virtual environment, so control feasibility is checked at each stage of geometric refinement. A Carbon-Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) curved shell with three Macro Fiber Composite (MFC) actuators is designed and evaluated entirely within this pre-fabrication phase. The FE model predicts a 4.821 mm baseline tip deflection under a representative 0.2 N load and 9.2 mm combined actuation authority at 1500 V. Model order reduction is reported by stage: modal truncation reduces the 165,652-DOF full-order model to 40 states and second-order balanced truncation further reduces this to a 10-state ROM. This reduced-order model and the control formulation are adopted from the authors' previously verifiedd design and reused here as a fixed verification baseline, tracking the target deflection within 1.33% under voltage and structural constraints. The novel contribution of this study is the SysML-based digital-twin traceability framework, together with a quantitative uncertainty-propagation analysis showing that the nominal 3.6% deflection margin may not survive the specified ±0.1 mm manufacturing tolerance, a finding not previously reported. Thirteen quantified limitations are reported, including the absence of a physical prototype, a formal placement optimization, and a comparison against conventional sequential design, which remains a priority for future work.

Four critical process variables-laser power (250–350 W), scan speed (700–1500 mm/s),layer thickness (40–60 μm), and hatch spacing (100 –150 μm) were systematically analyzed via Response SurfaceMethodology (RSM), and second-order predictive models were built to correlate these parameters with the resultingmechanical properties. Under optimal processing conditions, the fabricated specimens achieved peak values of 1195.69 MPa in tensile strength and 1284.45 MPa in flexural strength. Microstructural analysis, conducted using SEM, X-ray and EDX, revealed strong interlayer fusion, uniform distribution of alloying elements, and a low incidence of internal defects, while the material’s deformation characteristics were further evaluated through true stress–true strain curves and strainhardening behavior.

papers.title: Assessing early perioperative outcomes of minimally invasive posterior approach versus direct anterior approach total hip arthroplasty: a prospective comparative randomized study on blood and pain management
papers.abstract: The choice of the surgical technique while performing total hip arthroplasty (THA) is debated and no consensus exists on which minimally-invasive approach can provide more benefit in achieving enhanced recovery after surgery. The aim of the present study was to compare the early post-operative outcomes of minimally invasive posterolateral approach (Mis-PLA) Vs. direct anterior approach (DAA) in the treatment of primary hip osteoarthritis, with regard to blood loss and postoperative pain. The hypothesis was that mis-PLA, despite being less widely used than DAA, could offer significant advantages over the more popular alternative. Fifty patients treated with THA from 2022 to 2023 at a single Institution were prospectively recruited and randomly assigned to receive either the Mis-PLA or DAA THA. Surgeons and patients were aware of the group assignment, ata analysts were blinded to the allocation. Primary endpoints included intraoperative and postoperative blood loss and the blood transfusion rate. Secondary outcomes included pain assessment using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), operating time, length of stay (LOS), and perioperative complications. The DAA group was associated with significantly higher intraoperative blood loss (266.0 ± 202.4 mL) compared to the Mis-PLA group (157.2 ± 50.9 mL; p < 0.05). No significant differences in postoperative blood loss were observed between the two groups (DAA: 238.0 ± 104.4 mL; Mis-PLA: 195.8 ± 135.9 mL) ( p = 0.280). Patients in the DAA group had a higher transfusion rate (12%) than those in the Mis-PLA group (3%), although the difference did not reach statistical significance ( p = 0.610). No statistically significant differences were reported in VAS scores between the two groups on the first or third postoperative day ( p = 0.483, and p = 0.236, respectively), nor for LOS ( p = 0.667). The operating time was significantly longer in the DAA group (85.6 ± 12.5) compared to the Mis-PLA group (61.6 ± 13.7; p < 0.0001). No major complications were reported in either group. Compared to the DAA, the Mis-PLA could be a suitable option for surgeons aiming to minimize intraoperative blood loss and reduce operating time during THA. No statistically significant differences were reported between the two groupsconcerning postoperative blood loss, perioperative pain, length of hospital stay, or complication rates.

papers.title: Accelerated Formulation Screening of Multi-Component Bioinks via a Deep Learning-Integrated High-Throughput Gradient Printing Platform
papers.abstract: Abstract The development of performant multi-component bioinks is severely bottlenecked by the astronomical size of the possible design space and the inefficiency of empirical, trial-and-error experimentation. Existing high-throughput screening (HTS) methods, such as microarrays and droplet microfluidics, remain limited by discrete sampling, cell-unfriendly environments, and a lack of integrated analytics. Herein, a high-throughput gradient printing (HTGP) platform is employed to overcome these barriers by integrating continuous combinatorial bioprinting with deep learning-powered phenotyping. The HTGP system rapidly generates bioink libraries with gradients within a native three-dimensional hydrogel environment, preserving cell viability and enabling in situ, direct interrogation of cell-material interactions. Coupled with an automated neural network pipeline, the platform quantitatively deciphers complex relationships between bioink composition and cellular responses from massive images. Under the tested in vitro conditions, it identified a formulation that enhanced human umbilical vein endothelial cell (HUVEC) proliferation and spreading, as well as a candidate bioink that exhibited osteo-inductive potential by promoting osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Critically, the formulation identified through deep learning-assisted screening showed an enhanced early regenerative response in a rat periodontal bone defect model compared with the controls. The HTGP platform shifts from discrete testing to intelligent, continuous exploration, poised to accelerate the discovery of advanced biomaterials for personalized tissue engineering.

papers.title: Titanium trabecular 3D electron beam melting (EBM) printed cervical cages to promote rapid healing in cervical fusion. A prospective study
papers.abstract: Background: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) is widely used for treating degenerative cervical disc disease. Porous trabecular titanium (PTT), manufactured by electron beam melting (EBM) technology, has demonstrated excellent osteogenic and osteoinductive potential in vitro, but in vivo performance remains unclear. Methods: This level IIb, prospective cohort study included 26 patients undergoing one- to three-level ACDF using patented 3D EBM-printed PTT cages modelled by CAD/CAM technology. Primary outcome was fusion rate at 3 months, assessed by CT. Secondary outcomes included VAS pain scores and the Neck Disability Index (NDI) at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Results: Single-level fusion was performed in 14 patients (54%), two-level fusion in 9 patients (35%), and three-level fusion in 3 patients (11%). At the 3-month CT scan 18 (72%) patients showed radiographic signs of new bone formation (Goldschlager grade ≥1), of these, 8 patients (32%) had continuous bridging bone (grade 2) meeting the study’s pre-specified definition of fusion, while 10 patients (40%) showed non-continuous new bone (grade 1), At the 6-month follow-up, plain radiographs suggested fusion in 96% of patients. Mean radicular and axial VAS pain scores improved by 83% and 81%, respectively. Mean NDI scores improved by 76%. Fusion rates and clinical outcomes did not differ between patients undergoing different numbers of operated levels. Conclusions: 3D-EBM-printed porous trabecular titanium cages in ACDF were associated with early radiographic signs of osseointegration on CT at 3 months, and with apparent fusion on plain radiographs in the large majority of patients by 6 months, together with significant improvements in disability and pain scores. Larger, controlled studies are needed to confirm these early findings.

papers.title: Design and Experimental Validation of a Pressurized Laser Powder Bed Fusion Platform for Continuous Multilayer Processing
papers.abstract: Investigating pressure-dependent laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) requires equipment capable of performing repeated layer cycles in a sealed pressurized environment. This study describes a pressurized LPBF platform integrating internal powder feeding and recoating, external laser delivery, synchronized motion control, and recirculating gas flow. The platform has a nominal design-pressure limit of 20 bar absolute, which was not experimentally demonstrated as a multilayer operating condition. Ar builds comprising 200 programmed layers with a nominal height of 6 mm were completed at 1 and 3 bar in approximately 2 h per build. One block was characterized at each Ar pressure; repeated Archimedes measurements yielded relative densities of 99.58 ± 0.19% and 94.08 ± 0.50%, respectively, without establishing between-build variability. Separate experiments demonstrated multilayer LPBF processing in N2 up to 9 bar and stationary laser melting up to 15 bar. The mean final nitrogen content increased from 0.05985 to 0.09270 wt.% between 1 and 9 bar for multilayer specimens and from 0.1415 to 0.3505 wt.% between 1 and 15 bar for stationary-melted specimens. Pressure retention was assessed through mechanical-gauge observation rather than continuous time-resolved acquisition. The results document the machine’s initial multilayer processing capability and its potential for investigating pressure-dependent processing behavior; they do not establish full-range performance or pressure-induced densification enhancement.

papers.title: Intraoperative Measurement of Soft Tissue Tension in Canine Uncemented Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Abstract This study aimed to quantify the incremental tension forces encountered during trial and final reductions during total hip arthroplasty surgery; determine the contribution to final soft tissue tension of the tenorrhaphy of the partial tenotomy of the deep gluteal tendon during closure; develop an intraoperative protocol of soft tissue tension evaluation, describing the Shuck, Kick and External Rotator tests as subjective tools for assessing tension; and correlate this with short-term clinical outcome. Prospective case series including client-owned dogs presented for total hip arthroplasty. Collected data included signalment, intraoperative tension measurements during sequential trial head use and trial reductions, and short-term clinical outcome. Twenty hips (19 dogs) were included. The final soft tissue tension ranged from 70.6 to 182.4 N, with an average of 124.5 N. The Shuck test was repeatable and consistent. Tenorrhaphy of the deep gluteal tendon partial tenotomy using a continuous pattern suture of metric 3.5 polydioxanone produced a significant increase in the tension of the periprosthetic soft tissue envelope. The Shuck test was a reliable measurement of overall soft tissue tension across the prosthetic hip joint. Tenorrhaphy of the deep gluteal tendon significantly increases the final soft tissue tension. A systematic, intraoperative approach to tension measurement and evaluation during total hip replacement is suggested.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Taylor Cone Analysis for Electrospinning Process-Window Identification and Cell-Laden Nanofiber Scaffold Fabrication
papers.abstract: Abstract Electrospinning is a powerful biofabrication technique for constructing fibrous scaffolds that mimic extracellular matrix architectures. However, the process is highly nonlinear and involves strongly coupled parameters, making fiber architecture and biological performance difficult to control empirically and limits reproducibility. Most machine learning (ML) studies still focus on static correlations between processing parameters and outcomes rather than on dynamic modeling of electrospinning evolution and regulation, thereby hindering real-time, precise process control. Here, we establish a data-driven framework that links process parameters, Taylor cone geometry, and nanofiber/cell outcomes through high-speed imaging and ML. A custom image-processing pipeline is developed to automatically extract cone angle, height, and width from in situ images with improved accuracy via a rotating-ray–based geometric algorithm. Using datasets collected from three representative polymer systems (PVDF, PVB, and PEO), random forest models outperform support vector machine and minimum description length, achieving moderate-to-good prediction of Taylor cone descriptors (R²≈0.57-0.83) across varied voltages, flow rate, and needle–collector distances. We further extend this framework to PEO-based cell electrospinning. By correlating predicted cone geometries with experimentally measured viability of 293T cells and umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells, we identify a Taylor cone “safe window” that simultaneously stabilizes jet formation and preserves cell survival (>95%). Guided by this window, a bilayer cell-laden scaffold comprising a PVB support layer and a PEO–cell layer is fabricated with improved process robustness. This enables stable delivery of high-density, highly viable cells and facilitates the fabrication of three-dimensional cell-laden nanofiber scaffolds. Overall, this Taylor cone analysis, ML-guided strategy provides a quantitative framework for process-window identification in polymer and cell electrospinning, and may support future integration with real-time monitoring, online inference, and closed-loop control in intelligent biofabrication.

papers.title: Enhancing the Structural Integrity of 3D Bioprinted Urethral Grafts for Clinical Applications using GelMA-Fibrinogen Bioinks Infused with Human Primary Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract The demand for organ transplantation continues to grow, since the shortage of organ donors and complications associated with existing treatments remain. A promising alternative to transplantation is the implantation of artificial organs, which can be produced using 3D bioprinting technology. This approach offers the advantage of patient-specific solutions tailored to individual needs. Patients with urethral stricture or hypospadias who are unable to urinate require urethral reconstruction, which carries risks of complications and stricture recurrence. These patients may benefit from a tissue-engineered urethra fabricated using autologous cells and 3D bioprinting. Therefore, a printer setup for tubular structures was developed for 3D-Bioplotter, and a gelatin-fibrinogen-based bioink was optimised by supplementation with GelMA to enhance mechanical properties suitable for clinical applications while maintaining cell compatibility. Tensile testing, printability, suturability, and cell viability analyses were performed to assess the outcomes of the different ink compositions. An artificial urethral graft was successfully printed, using our rod-based printer setup, and the GelMA-fibrinogen hydrogel exhibited an increase in Young's modulus compared with gelatin-fibrinogen hydrogel. Further, the 5% GelMA-fibrinogen hydrogel also exhibited good suturability and maintained cell viability after 14 days in culture. Human urothelial and smooth muscle cells developed characteristic morphologies within the print, and a 210% increase in burst pressure was observed for the urethral graft after 14 days in tissue culture, compared with the acellular graft. Our 3D bioprinted artificial urethra herein, containing an inner layer of human urothelial cells stabilised with polycaprolactone and an outer ring of smooth muscle cells, represents a significant step forward in replicating natural urethral architecture for developing grafts as new treatment options for urethral disorders.

papers.title: Bioinspired Mechano‐Chemical Titanium Interfaces With Potential for Infection‐Resistant Osseointegration
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Bacterial colonization and insufficient osseointegration remain major challenges for titanium‐based orthopedic and dental implants. Here, we developed a bioinspired mechano‐chemical titanium interface by combining an anodization‐derived micro‐/nano‐pitted topography with a polydopamine–citric acid–quercetin (PCQ) functional layer. Inspired by dragonfly‐wing micro‐/nanostructures, the resulting OPT@PCQ interface exhibited hierarchical topography, enhanced hydrophilicity, and preserved overall mechanical response. OPT@PCQ showed favorable cytocompatibility and significantly promoted osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow‐derived mesenchymal stromal cells, with increased alkaline phosphatase activity, matrix mineralization, and RUNX2, COL1A1, and OCN expression. It also displayed pronounced antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli , accompanied by bacterial morphological deformation and reduced viability. Transcriptomic analysis of S. aureus revealed broad perturbation of central carbon metabolism, glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, ribosome‐associated processes, and stress‐response pathways. In vivo, OPT@PCQ promoted wound closure and markedly enhanced new bone formation and trabecular reconstruction in a noninfected rat femoral defect model. Qualitative hemolysis assessment and major‐organ histology provided preliminary evidence of hemocompatibility and systemic biosafety under the tested conditions. Collectively, these findings support OPT@PCQ as a multifunctional titanium interface with potential for infection‐resistant osseointegration; however, direct validation in an infected bone‐defect model remains necessary.

papers.title: A mechanistic theory of planning in prefrontal cortex
papers.abstract: Abstract Planning is critical for adaptive behaviour in a changing world, because it lets us anticipate the future and adjust our actions accordingly. While prefrontal cortex is crucial for this process, it remains unknown how planning is implemented in neural circuits. Prefrontal representations were recently discovered in simpler sequence memory tasks, where different populations of neurons represent different future time points. We demonstrate that combining such representations with the ubiquitous principle of neural attractor dynamics allows circuits to solve much richer problems including planning. This is achieved by embedding the environment structure directly in synaptic connections to implement an attractor network that infers desirable futures. The resulting ‘spacetime attractor’ excels at planning in challenging tasks known to depend on prefrontal cortex. Recurrent neural networks trained by gradient descent on such tasks learn a solution that precisely recapitulates the spacetime attractor – in representation, in dynamics, and in connectivity. Analyses of networks trained across different environment structures reveal a generalisation mechanism that rapidly reconfigures the world model used for planning, without the need for synaptic plasticity. The spacetime attractor is a testable mechanistic theory of planning. If true, it would provide a path towards detailed mechanistic understanding of how prefrontal cortex structures adaptive behaviour.

papers.title: Reallocation of nonlocal entanglement in incommensurate cold atom arrays
papers.abstract: Cold atom arrays in optical lattices offer a highly tunable platform for exploring complex quantum phenomena that are difficult to realize in conventional materials. Here, we investigate the emergence of controllable long-range quantum correlations in a simulated twisted bilayer structure with fermionic cold atoms. By exploiting the incommensurate nature of the twisted bilayer, we observe a significant enhancement of long-range susceptibility, suggesting the formation of stable entangled states between spatially distant localized spins. We further show that the tunability of the interlayer coupling in terms of driving fields enables us to manipulate these entangled states without deformation of lattice structure and extra doping. Our findings provide a pathway for overcoming challenges in establishing strong correlations across distant sites, highlighting the potential of optical lattices as a versatile platform for advanced quantum technologies.

papers.title: CarBench: A comprehensive benchmark for neural surrogates on high-fidelity 3D car aerodynamics
papers.abstract: Abstract Benchmarking has been the cornerstone of progress in computer vision, natural language processing, and the broader deep learning domain, driving algorithmic innovation through standardized datasets and reproducible evaluation protocols. The growing availability of large-scale Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) datasets has opened new opportunities for applying machine learning to aerodynamic and engineering design. Yet, despite this progress, large-scale standardized benchmarks remain limited for high-resolution three-dimensional automotive aerodynamics, making it difficult to evaluate and compare models systematically. In this work, we introduce CarBench, a large-scale standardized benchmark dedicated to high-resolution 3D automotive aerodynamics, and perform a large-scale evaluation of state-of-the-art models on DrivAerNet++, the largest public dataset for automotive aerodynamics, containing over 8,000 high-fidelity car simulations. We assess eleven representative model configurations spanning multiple modeling paradigms: classical neural operator methods (e.g., Fourier Neural Operator), geometric deep learning approaches (PointNet, RegDGCNN, PointMAE, PointTransformer), transformer-based neural solvers (Transolver, Transolver++, AB-UPT), and implicit field networks leveraging triplane representations (TripNet). Beyond standard interpolation tasks, we perform cross-category experiments in which representative transformer-based solvers trained on a single car archetype are evaluated on unseen categories to probe generalization. Our analysis covers predictive accuracy, pressure-field fidelity relative to the CFD reference, computational efficiency, and statistical uncertainty in evaluation metrics, providing a unified comparison across modeling families and quantifying the robustness of performance estimates under shifts in test geometry distributions. To accelerate progress in data-driven engineering, we open-source the complete benchmark framework, including training pipelines, metric-level uncertainty estimation routines based on bootstrap resampling, and pretrained model weights, establishing a reproducible foundation for large-scale learning from high-fidelity external automotive aerodynamics simulations, available at https://github.com/Mohamedelrefaie/CarBench .

papers.title: Calibrated uncertainty quantification for prosumer flexibility aggregation in ancillary service markets
papers.abstract: Reliable forecasting of prosumer flexibility is critical for demand response aggregators participating in frequency controlled ancillary service markets, where reliability requirements such as the P90 standard are enforced. Limited behavioural data and dependence on exogenous forecasts introduce uncertainty into flexibility estimates, which can lead to reserve overestimation and financial penalties. This study applies and systematically evaluates established uncertainty quantification approaches based on Monte Carlo dropout (MCD), conformal prediction (CP), and conformalised quantile regression (CQR) to construct prediction intervals for aggregated prosumer flexibility and support uncertainty-aware aggregator bidding. The approaches are evaluated for a behind-the-meter aggregator participating in the Danish manual frequency restoration reserve capacity market. A large-scale synthetic dataset is generated using an industry-grade home energy management system, combined with publicly available load, solar, price, activation, and device-level data. Multiple multivariate CP strategies are evaluated using MCD predictions, alongside CQR using a separately trained quantile regression model. Under nominal synthetic test conditions, conformal methods substantially improve joint coverage compared with uncalibrated MCD baselines. More conservative methods satisfy the 90% lower-tail reliability requirement, while CQR and MCP provide comparatively narrow intervals and higher retained economic value. CQR and MCP retain approximately 69% and 68% of perfect-information profit, respectively, under the stricter penalty interpretation. A controlled robustness analysis further shows that increasing perturbations of load, solar, price, and activation inputs increase overbidding and reduce empirical coverage and economic performance. The results highlight the trade-off between reliability, economic value, and robustness to input uncertainty when applying established uncertainty quantification approaches to aggregator bidding.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Free Energy Calculations by Generalized Hierarchical Bayesian Inference
papers.abstract: Abstract Free energy calculations are routinely used to study molecular processes inaccessible to unbiased molecular dynamics, but their utility ultimately depends on knowing when and how much their predictions can be trusted. Uncertainty estimation is therefore essential for distinguishing genuine physical features of a free energy profile from artifacts arising from limited simulation data or inadequate sampling. Gaussian processes have emerged as a powerful framework for reconstructing free energy profiles together with predictive uncertainties. However, existing implementations typically condition on fixed hyperparameters and observation noise, preventing predictive uncertainties from adapting to the information content of the simulation data. Here, we develop a generalized hierarchical Gaussian process framework that accounts for these neglected sources of uncertainty. Applications to umbrella sampling and extended Lagrangian metadynamics of peptide-lipid membrane interactions demonstrate that the resulting uncertainty estimates track reconstruction errors across a wide range of sampling and data conditions.

papers.title: WSM-Aware HRI: An IoT-Enhanced Framework for Early Detection and Norm-Guided Repair of Failures with LLM Guidance
papers.abstract: Human–robot interaction (HRI) failures remain a major barrier to deploying robots in real-world environments. Prior work often treats failures as isolated technical faults or focuses on post-hoc recovery behaviors. In practice, many breakdowns arise because humans and robots operate under inconsistent assumptions about the current world state. We propose WSM-Aware HRI, an IoT-enhanced modular framework that unifies diverse HRI breakdowns as World-State Mismatches (WSMs) between a human's instruction-implied assumptions and a robot's grounded world model built from multimodal perception and digital augmentation. A Large Language Model (LLM) is used to make implicit assumptions explicit, map them to a small set of mismatch types, and specify the evidence needed for verification against the robot's world state. WSM-Aware HRI shifts failure handling from execution-time recovery to proactive mismatch detection during intention formation, enabling interventions guided by safety, norm compliance, and multi-user coordination with transparent explanations. We evaluate mismatch identification in ten everyday cases spanning both visual and latent-state mismatches. The system can accurately produce the expected output results, and ablations show that reliable identification depends on appropriate grounding representations and verification-oriented refinement. These results indicate that treating interaction breakdowns as explicit world–state mismatches enables earlier detection of impending failures and offers a principled mechanism for integrating external evidence and social constraints into human–robot interaction.
