papers.title: Active-Labeling Evaluation for Computer Agriculture Nematode-Cyst Detection Under Sparse Soil-Sample Ground Truth: An Artificial Intelligence Annotation-Efficiency Bound
papers.abstract: Active learning promises to reduce the annotation burden of training nematode-cyst detection models for precision agriculture, but the size of that reduction is not known when ground truth comes from sparse soil samples rather than exhaustive visual inspection. the present analysis derives an annotation-efficiency bound for pool-based active learning under sparse soil-sample ground truth. The detection task is formalised as a two-stage process in which a classifier selects candidate cysts from soil imagery and a laboratory assay confirms a small labelled subset. Under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, the bound is evaluated across a design grid of 8, 16, 24 and 32 clusters and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, with 2000 replications per cell. The annotation-efficiency gain is bounded by the ratio of label noise to cluster-level variance, and that 52 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point improvement at 80% power. The bound provides a design rule for allocating annotation effort between active selection and confirmatory soil sampling.

papers.title: Active-Learning Query Synthesis for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Soil-Nutrient Inference Under Laboratory Assay Budget Caps: A Computer Information-Gain Regret Bound
papers.abstract: Soil-nutrient inference from spectral and proximal sensing is constrained less by model capacity than by the cost of laboratory assays used to label training queries. the present analysis formalises budget-capped active learning for soil-nutrient regression as a sequential decision problem and derives a finite-horizon information-gain regret bound for a query-synthesis policy that selects assay locations by maximising expected reduction in posterior predictive entropy per unit assay cost. The bound decomposes cumulative regret into an information-gain term, a cost-normalisation term and a misspecification residual, and it predicts that regret grows as the square root of the assay budget rather than linearly in the number of candidate locations. The derivation is connected to the computer-science literature on active learning, Gaussian-process bandits and cost-sensitive information acquisition, and its assumptions are stated explicitly so that the bound can be falsified by future field evaluation. The contribution is a formal, testable statement of when cost-aware query synthesis is provably preferable to uniform or random assay allocation under a fixed laboratory budget, together with the boundary conditions under which the guarantee fails.

papers.title: Mathematical foundations of artificial intelligence in healthcare: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare relies on diverse mathematical frameworks, yet their contributions to model development, evaluation, interpretability, and clinical translation remain fragmented. This systematic review synthesized the classical and emerging mathematical foundations underpinning healthcare AI and examined major methodological and application trends. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, studies published between January 2016 and June 30, 2026, were identified through systematic searches of Scopus, Google Scholar, and PubMed/MEDLINE, with searches conducted using Harzing’s Publish or Perish v8 where applicable. Bibliometric analysis was performed using VOSviewer, while methodological quality was assessed using an adapted JBI-based framework and AMSTAR-2 for systematic reviews. Of 653 records identified, 147 studies met the eligibility criteria. Non-mutually exclusive mathematical-domain coding identified linear algebra in 100/147 studies (68.0%), calculus and optimization in 91/147 (61.9%), and probability and statistics in 79/147 (53.7%), highlighting their roles in data representation, learning, optimization, inference, uncertainty quantification, and validation. A separate mutually exclusive classification of dominant methodological themes identified explainable and trustworthy AI in 24/147 studies (16.3%), statistics and learning theory in 23/147 (15.6%), probability and Bayesian methods in 23/147 (15.6%), calculus and optimization in 19/147 (12.9%), and linear algebra in 15/147 (10.2%). Radiology and medical imaging were the leading healthcare application (24.3%), while classification and diagnosis were the most frequent clinical task (17.1%). Overall, healthcare AI is supported by an interconnected mathematical ecosystem. Emerging approaches, including graph neural networks, Transformers, and quantum machine learning, require stronger external validation, standardized benchmarking, and rigorous evaluation for reliable clinical translation.

papers.title: Empirical-Constraint Physics-Informed Neural Network for Predicting the Height of Water-Conducting Fracture Zone
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of water-conducting fracture zone (WCFZ) height is essential for preventing mine water hazards. Existing empirical, numerical, and artificial intelligence methods are limited by applicability, parameter sensitivity, or insufficient incorporation of engineering prior knowledge. This study develops a physics-informed neural network (PINN) using 107 measured datasets from North China-type coalfields. Overburden lithology, mining height, mining depth, and working face length are used as inputs. Empirical formulas from China’s “Three-Under” coal mining regulations are converted into interval constraints and incorporated into the loss function, while Bayesian optimization determines key hyperparameters. The model converges stably and achieves coefficients of determination above 0.93 for both training and testing sets, with root mean square error values of 5.717 m and 4.330 m for the training and testing sets, respectively, and mean absolute error values below 4 m. It outperforms empirical formulas, backpropagation neural networks, and deep neural networks without the empirical-constraint term. For the 11201 working face in a Shanxi mine, the predicted WCFZ height is 85.51 m, with a relative error of 1.71%. These results support the use of soft empirical constraints to improve prediction accuracy and engineering reliability, providing technical support for WCFZ height prediction and mine water hazard prevention in North China-type coalfields.

papers.title: Certified Shift-Aware Uncertainty Quantification for Artificial Intelligence Seasonal Precipitation Forecasts Under Volcanic Aerosol Injection: Coverage Bounds and Famine Early-Warning Trigger Reliability
papers.abstract: Volcanic aerosol injection could alter seasonal precipitation patterns in ways that existing artificial intelligence (AI) forecast systems have never encountered, yet famine early-warning triggers built on those forecasts carry no formal reliability guarantee under such distributional shift. The framework combines a divergence-based shift detector, a distributionally robust conformal prediction layer, and a trigger reliability calculus that maps forecast intervals to famine early-warning activation probabilities. Formal results establish that the coverage gap under shift is bounded by the total variation distance between source and target distributions, that the trigger false-alarm rate is controlled at a user-specified level, and that the bound is tight in a minimax sense. The analysis is methodological and theoretical: no empirical forecast data are analysed, and the framework is presented as a certified design that would require validation against reanalysis and observational records before operational deployment. The contribution is a set of coverage and reliability guarantees that make the epistemic status of famine triggers explicit under a forcing scenario for which no historical training analogue exists.

papers.title: Estimation and optimal design for constant stress model under maximum ranked set sampling with unequal samples
papers.abstract: This paper develops an optimal design for a constant stress model under Maximum Ranked Set Sampling with Unequal Samples (MaxRSSU) which is a novel approach to improve estimation efficiency in life test studies. The maximum likelihood and Bayesian methods are used to estimate model parameters and reliability characteristics. Subsequently, the asymptotic and highest posterior density intervals (HPD) are constructed for quantifying uncertainty quantification. A comprehensive simulation study is conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed estimators, followed by an application to real-life reliability data. Finally, optimal sample allocation plans are formulated under the MaxRSSU methodology with multiple optimality criteria by minimizing posterior variance. The studied design strategy emphasizes the benefit of MaxRSSU over the traditional simple random sampling technique, thus providing more efficient information for reliability engineering study.

papers.title: Calibration-Free Uncertainty Quantification for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Crop Disease Triage Under Label Shift: A Computer Conformal Risk-Control Evaluation
papers.abstract: Crop disease triage systems that route leaf images to agronomists must control the risk of missed infection when deployed across regions whose pathogen mix differs from the training distribution. Calibration-based uncertainty scores are widely used for this purpose, but they presuppose that the label marginal is stable, an assumption that fails under the label shift characteristic of seasonal and geographic deployment. The framework is evaluated through a replication-based design study of the before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64), with power estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points.54 clusters are required for 80% power at a 5-percentage-point effect, and that the conformal threshold attains finite-sample risk control without any calibration step. The contribution is a shift-robust triage rule whose guarantee is a coverage statement rather than a probability statement, together with a design-characterisation that tells field evaluators how many clusters their before-after-control-impact trial needs.

papers.abstract: Maraging steel is a high-strength material with enhanced mechanical properties. Mössbauer spectroscopy (MS), also known as recoilless nuclear gamma resonance, can be used to study the surface and bulk of a material. Conversion X-ray Mössbauer spectroscopy (CXMS) and conversion electron Mössbauer spectroscopy (CEMS) provide information about the structure of materials at different depths: 10 µm and 0.3 µm, respectively. This method can reveal information about the inhomogeneity of the material's surface layer. In this research, the study samples were made from 1.2709 maraging steel metal powder using selective laser melting (SLM). The initial samples were in the shape of a cylinder with 25 mm diameter and 5 mm height. After 3D printing, the surface of the studied samples was subjected to a post-production treatment process. The samples were studied under the following conditions: after sandblasting; after sandblasting and annealing at 500 °C in air, after polishing; and after polishing and annealing at 500 °C in air. Studies of the phase composition and phase transformations of 1.2709 maraging steel have revealed the relation between surface treatment methods and phase distribution. A detailed investigation of the surface of the sample revealed that the initial sandblasted and polished samples contained martensite and retained austenite phases. The phase composition in the surface layer is also affected by the surface treatment method. While the polished sample showed only the martensitic phase, sandblasting preserved both the austenitic and martensitic phases. The samples exposed to temperature also show the presence of iron oxide (α-Fe2O3) at a depth of around 10 μm. Studies of the thin surface layer at depth between 0.1 and 0.4 μm have revealed that the surface is inhomogeneous. A polished surface tends to create the α-Fe2O3 oxide when exposed to temperature, whereas a sandblasted surface is covered with γ-Fe2O3.

papers.title: Realizing uniform implosion of double-cone ignition by combining a predictive model and Bayesian optimization
papers.abstract: Abstract The direct-drive inertial confinement fusion (ICF) schemes like the double-cone ignition (DCI) scheme can efficiently utilize the laser energy, while it faces significant challenges in uniform implosion and achieving high areal density of the fuel. This is because of the P2 asymmetry driven by the laser and the high-mode Rayleigh-Taylor instability (RTI) growth. We propose an efficient optimization approach by integrating multiple algorithms and physical models to address these limitations. Based on two-dimensional (2D) radiation hydrodynamics simulations, a scaling law for the areal density is derived, incorporating laser parameters, target structure, and instability factors, all of which have significant effects on the areal density. The Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is employed to optimize the irradiation positions and spot radius of the two-ring laser, improving the uniformity of laser intensity distribution on the target surface and thus reducing the P2 asymmetry. Combining one-dimensional (1D) simulations with the RTI growth theory, a quantitative predictive model for P2 asymmetry and a qualitative predictive model for high-mode RTI are established, significantly reducing computational costs. Finally, the outputs of the predictive models are used as input parameters to perform Bayesian optimization for iteratively optimizing laser profile and target structure. The areal density of the DCI in 2D simulations increases from 0.156 g/cm² to 0.274 g/cm² with 2 ×16 kJ drive lasers. This method provides a new paradigm for the experimental design of DCI and polar direct-drive (PDD) scheme.

papers.title: Calibration-Free Uncertainty Quantification for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Disease Diagnosis Under Cross-Site Reagent Variation: A Computer Coverage-Regret Evaluation
papers.abstract: Cross-site reagent variation in plant disease diagnostic pipelines can shift the operating characteristics of artificial intelligence classifiers in ways that post-hoc calibration cannot anticipate, because the calibration map is estimated on source-site data and applied unchanged to target sites whose reagent chemistry differs. the present analysis formalises the problem as a distribution shift in the feature-conditional label distribution induced by reagent batch effects, and proposes a calibration-free uncertainty quantification procedure that replaces the post-hoc calibration map with a coverage-regret criterion evaluated directly on the target site. The procedure is a distribution-free conformal predictor whose nonconformity scores are computed from a reagent-invariant representation, and whose coverage guarantee is stated as a regret bound against the nominal level. A replication-based evaluation was conducted: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2), and the behaviour of the ordinary least squares estimator was characterised under that process. The estimated bias for the intercept was -0.0248 and for the exposure coefficient 0.00022; the root mean squared error was 0.87656 for the intercept and 0.01611 for the exposure coefficient; empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that under the declared process the estimator is essentially unbiased and that nominal coverage is attained, which establishes the reference behaviour against which the coverage-regret criterion is to be benchmarked. The contribution is a formal criterion and a proposed procedure, not a validated field deployment.

papers.title: Mössbauer spectroscopy for additive manufacturing be selective laser melting
papers.abstract: Various experimental techniques (X-ray diffraction - XRD, scanning electron microscopy - SEM, energy dispersive spectroscopy - EDS) were used to improve the SLM process and to inspect the properties (surface morphology, microstructure, phase and elemental composition) of components produced by SLM. Mössbauer spectroscopy (MS) is a suitable method for examining iron-based components. Transmission 57Fe MS (TMS) can be used for investigation of metal powders. Backscattering 57Fe MS with registered conversion electrons (CEMS) and secondary X-rays (CXMS) allows surface layers to be studied selectively. When applying CEMS, we receive information from the surface layer with a depth of about 0.3 μm. The CXMS contains information from depths of tens of micrometers. The phase composition of stainless steel metal powders (CL20ES) and maraging steel powders (CL50WS) during annealing was studied by TMS in the temperature range of 500 - 1100 °C in air and in an inert atmosphere. Different iron oxides (α-Fe2O3, Fe3O4 and wüstite) were identified after thermal treatment in air at different temperatures. Depending on the annealing temperature in a nitrogen atmosphere, transformations of austenite ↔ martensite were observed. CXMS and CEMS showed changes in the phase composition of the parts depending on the annealing temperature and atmosphere. At the same time, some changes occur only in the surface layer with a thickness of approximately 0.3 μm. These are changes in the ratio of the austenitic and ferritic phases. Various iron oxides also occur during surface oxidation. In accordance with XRD and EDS, it has been shown that some phase transformations occur as a result of the diffusion of alloying elements in the surface layers. SEM showed an inhomogeneity of the emerging surface layer, which unfortunately results in difficulties in the registration of CEMS spectra.

papers.title: A SINGLE INDUCTOR MULTI-PORT POWERCONVERTER FED PMSM USING CONTROLLER OPTIMIZATION TECHNIQUES FOR EV APPLICATIONS
papers.abstract: The integration of renewable generation and energy storage into electric-vehicle propulsion systems requires a power-conversion structure capable of coordinating multiple energy paths with limited hardware.This work investigates an EV drive configuration in which a single-inductor multi-port DC-DC converter interfaces a photovoltaic source and a battery with the propulsion DC link.A voltage-source inverter supplies a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM), and an artificial neural network assisted model predictive control (ANN-MPC) strategy is employed for motor-drive control.The predictive controller evaluates the motor response and determines appropriate inverter switching actions, while the neural-network component assists the controller in representing nonlinear operating behavior.The complete configuration is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink and examined for different source, battery, and motor operating conditions.The obtained simulation results are used to evaluate source-side power transfer, battery operation, converter current behavior, and PMSM tracking performance.The study demonstrates the feasibility of combining a multi-source converter with ANN-MPC based PMSM control in an EV-oriented powertrain

papers.title: Mechanical Behavior of a Novel Nonuniform Gyroid Metamaterial Under Quasi‐Static Loading
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surfaces have become ideal templates for fabricating porous materials with customized properties owing to excellent geometric tunability. Herein, a novel nonuniform Gyroid lattice with an innovative “X”‐shaped reinforced domain is proposed to improve the quasi‐static compressive performance of uniform Gyroid lattices. Uniform Gyroid (UG) and nonuniform reinforced Gyroid (XG) lattices made of Ti─6Al─4V are fabricated by selective laser melting, and their quasi‐static mechanical properties are comprehensively characterized and analyzed via experiments and numerical simulations. The experimental results demonstrate that properly designed XG configurations achieve superior comprehensive mechanical performance compared with the UG lattice. Adjusting the width of the reinforced domain exerts significant effects on specific elastic modulus, specific initial peak stress, and specific plateau stress, while rotating the reinforced domain obviously affects specific energy absorption (SEA). Further numerical investigations reveal that within the range of the investigated structural parameters, the optimal reinforced domain width and rotation angle are 9/40 and 45°, respectively, to achieve maximum SEA. These findings can provide valuable insights and design guidance for developing high‐performance triply periodic minimal surfaces lattice structures.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Bayesian Optimization for Artificial Intelligence Climate Model Parameter Tuning Under Sparse Observational Constraints: Convergence Bounds and Ensemble Forecast Fidelity
papers.abstract: The calibration of artificial intelligence climate models against sparse observational records remains a bottleneck for ensemble forecast fidelity, particularly in regions where station coverage is thin. The framework is illustrated on a real reanalysis record for Nairobi, Kenya: NASA POWER monthly MERRA-2 air temperature at 2 m, 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 20.146 °C, a standard deviation of 1.094 °C, and a linear warming trend of 0.2477 °C per decade. The convergence analysis establishes that the expected simple regret of the proposed acquisition rule decays at a rate governed by the smoothness of the prior and the effective dimension of the parameter space, and that the bound is tight up to logarithmic factors. The Nairobi record is used to demonstrate how the bound translates into a practical evaluation budget for a low-dimensional calibration problem, and to show that the resulting ensemble retains fidelity to the observed trend. The contribution is a formal bridge between the sample-efficiency theory of Bayesian optimization and the calibration practice of AI climate models under observational sparsity.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network Emulation of Convective Storm Initiation over the Sahel: Calibration Bounds and Warning-Lead-Time Equity for Climate Analytics
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a computationally tractable route to emulating convective storm initiation over the Sahel, where sparse observations and coarse numerical weather prediction limit warning lead times. The framework combines a physics-informed residual formulation of the convective initiation problem with a distributionally robust calibration bound derived from the PINN's training residual and a warning-lead-time equity functional defined over population-weighted exposure. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-derived temperature record for Kampala, Uganda (NASA POWER MERRA-2, 2000–2023, 312 monthly observations, mean 22.443 °C, trend −0.1564 °C per decade), which serves as a calibration anchor for the environmental-state distribution. Calibration bounds and equity bounds must be co-designed: a PINN that is accurate on average can still violate lead-time equity, and an equity-constrained PINN may require a tighter physics residual than accuracy alone would demand. The contribution is a formal bridge between physics-informed emulation and distributive climate analytics, with implications for the design of early-warning systems in data-sparse regions.

papers.title: Guidelines for Space, Earth Observation, and AAM AI-based Solution Development
papers.abstract: A set of guidelines is presented for the responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence in Advanced Air Mobility, space systems, and space-based Earth Observation. AI applications are examined across onboard and ground-based environments, including perception, detect-and-avoid, guidance and control, autonomous decision-making, satellite data processing, change detection, and geospatial foundation models. The principal barriers to operational adoption are identified, demonstrating that technical performance alone is insufficient without explainability, traceability, uncertainty quantification, physical consistency, representative datasets, domain-shift evaluation, human oversight, and deterministic fallback mechanisms. Drawing on evolving EASA and FAA guidance, the EU AI Act, and relevant aerospace assurance standards, recommendations are provided for early regulatory engagement, incremental deployment, rigorous simulation and validation, runtime monitoring, and comprehensive model and data documentation. The analysis concludes by highlighting the technical, transparency, accuracy, and trust challenges involved in deploying AI across space, urban air mobility, and Earth observation. It emphasizes that early compliance with evolving regulations and sustained collaboration among industry, researchers, and authorities are essential for responsible, effective real-world adoption.

papers.title: The impact of gamification on language learning: a Quasi-experimental study in higher education
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the role of gamification, conceptualized as a reflective lesson improvement cycle in the areas of engagement, motivation and language proficiency at the higher education level. Design/methodology/approach A quasi-experimental design spanning 14 weeks was conducted with 300 undergraduate university students as part of a collaborative lesson study process consisting of a cyclical process of: plan, teach, reflect. Statistical analysis was conducted with the use of ANOVA, Cohen’s d and Kruskal–Wallis tests. Findings The findings showed significant improvement in all language skill areas, with a large effect size (d = 1.37) suggesting gamification made a considerable contribution to engagement and learning outcomes for the students. Research limitations/implications This study was conducted at one university, and involved a 14-week intervention. These factors may limit the generalization of findings. Although we employed appropriate statistical analyses (ANOVA, Cohen’s d, Kruskal–Wallis), more extensive longitudinal studies are necessary to confirm the meaning of sustained findings. Qualitative understanding related to teachers’ reflections could add depth to contextual understandings. Nevertheless, these findings signal a route by which reflective, gamified learning cycles can inform evidence-based approaches to instructional reform, and drive experimental research on language education and engagement-oriented pedagogical innovation. Practical implications The results suggest that using gamification in a reflective lesson-study framework has a positive impact on student motivation, engagement and language proficiency. Educators can implement the plan–teach–reflect cycle to enhance lessons by addition integration of game-like components such as; levels and badges, and include feedback to improve lessons in a continual means, while higher education institutions could integrate this into professional learning programs, allowing for teachers use of gamified reflection, as a data-informed application, to improve teaching quality viewed as fostering active learning in varied contexts at higher education institutions. Social implications Gamification encourages students to experience inclusion, collaboration and empowerment through the reflective cycle of gamification experiences within higher education. The collaborative structure of gamification experiences allows for teamwork, self-reflection and accountability. Collaborative activities promote building resilience, creativity and social/environmental responsibility – core competencies for education around Industry 5.0. Gamification experiences strengthen the academic and interpersonal dimensions, making it easier for students to experience challenges as areas of growth. As a socially engaged pedagogical model, gamification promotes equity, engagement and human-centered learning, and supports global commitments to adaptive, sustainable educational reform initiatives. Originality/value This study provides context-rich, practice-oriented evidence from a 14-week, multi-component gamified language intervention in higher education (n = 300). This investigation adds to predominantly short-term literature by examining longer-term implementation across layers-including sustainable engagement over practice in speaking, listening, reading and writing, and plotting out how a lesson-study cycle hones instruction iteratively. The study does not isolate individual game mechanics; it evaluates the entire instructional package in a real-life classroom environment.

papers.title: Mapping Emerging Trends in Artificial Intelligence for Quality Control and Management: A Large‐Scale Computational Literature Review Using Semantic Natural Language Processing
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of artificial intelligence into industrial quality control (QC) and management encompassing automated defect detection, real‐time process monitoring, and zero‐defect manufacturing has generated a rapidly expanding yet fragmented research landscape. This study addresses the need for comprehensive mapping of quality and reliability engineering practice through a computational systematic review of 9618 publications spanning the 2020–2025 period. A hybrid natural language processing (NLP) pipeline combining FlashText, Sentence‐BERT, KeyBERT, and spaCy performs semantic extraction of AI architectures, learning paradigms, defect typologies, and deployment contexts. The review pursues three objectives: mapping the architectural evolution of deep learning in industrial inspection, characterizing operational challenges of AI‐driven manufacturing, and identifying methodological frontiers for improving production reliability and supporting intelligent quality assurance (QA) systems. Results reveal that AI‐based quality control advances through coevolution of neural architectures, learning paradigms, and deployment requirements. CNNs remain central to discriminative visual inspection, while Transformers extend capabilities for multimodal reasoning. The field exhibits strong bias toward surface defects while overlooking safety‐critical internal defects. Emerging trends show transition from algorithm‐centric research toward deployment‐oriented paradigms including Uncertainty Quantification, Edge AI, Explainable AI, and Digital Twins. This work provides practitioners with an evidence‐based foundation for developing reliable, scalable AI quality systems aligned with Industry 4.0 principles.

papers.title: Enhanced laser-driven directional neutron source via Bayesian optimization of cone targets
papers.abstract: Abstract Laser-driven neutron sources, particularly beam-target neutron sources, hold significant potential for applications in neutron radiography, non-destructive inspection, nuclear astrophysics, etc. However, the quality of current beam-target neutron sources, especially neutron yield and divergence angle, still requires substantial improvement. Here, we present a novel laser-driven cone-target scheme to enhance the quality of neutron beams. Through integrated two-dimensional (2D) particle-in-cell (PIC) and Monte Carlo (MC) simulations, it is demonstrated that the proposed scheme significantly enhances the ion acceleration by effectively focusing the laser pulse and guiding the electron beams. With the resulting increase in ion energy, a number of neutrons per laser shot of about 2.0×10 9 is achieved, which is 39 times higher than that from the plane target. Moreover, the scheme raises the forward-to-sideward yield ratio and makes the emission of the high-energy neutrons more forward-directed. Our theoretical model systematically elucidates the physical mechanisms governing high-energy ion generation, neutron yield enhancement and forward-emission optimization. Assisted by Bayesian Optimization, the influences of the target and laser parameters are also investigated and the optimal parameter ranges are identified, facilitating the experimental demonstration of laser-driven directional neutron sources.

papers.title: Physics-Constrained Neural Network Deep Learning Model for Predicting Residual Flexural Strengths of Steel Fibre Reinforced Concrete: A Multi-Study Generalisation Framework
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of residual flexural strengths is essential for the structural design and performance assessment of steel fibre reinforced concrete (SFRC). While machine learning models have recently demonstrated strong predictive capability, most of the existing approaches rely on heuristic feature selection, unconstrained architectures, and random validation splits that may overestimate generalisation capacity. This study proposes a Hard-Constrained Physics-Informed Neural Network (PCNN) for predicting the residual flexural strengths fR1–fR4 of steel fibre reinforced concrete (SFRC). Non-negativity, monotonic dependence on the reinforcement index, and bounded sequential evolution across crack mouth opening displacement (CMOD) stages are enforced architecturally through custom layers, guaranteeing mechanical admissibility by construction. The model was trained and validated on 235 original beam specimens from 18 experimental groups (expanded to 860 via controlled integer replication) using GroupKFold by Study cross-validation to eliminate data leakage. PCNN achieves fR1 MAE = 1.256 MPa and R2 = 0.606 across held-out experimental campaigns, competitive with Ridge Regression (MAE = 1.144, R2 = 0.688). Monotonicity audits show a 0% violation rate for PCNN versus 7.3% and 10.2% for Random Forest and GBDT, respectively. PCNN is the only model in the comparison that guarantees physical admissibility for all possible input configurations. The results demonstrate that embedding mechanical principles directly into neural network architecture enhances robustness and interpretability without compromising accuracy. The proposed Physics-Informed Neural Networks framework provides a transferable methodology for physics-guided machine learning in structural materials modelling.

papers.title: dpdata: A Scalable Python Toolkit for Atomistic Machine Learning Data Sets
papers.abstract: Seamless management of atomistic data sets is a critical prerequisite for the successful development and deployment of machine learning potentials (MLPs). Here, we present dpdata, an open-source Python library designed to streamline every aspect of MLP data handling. Built upon a flexible, plugin-based architecture, dpdata supports reading, writing, and converting between a broad range of file formats─from popular quantum-chemistry packages and molecular-dynamics engines to specialized MLP frameworks. Users may define custom data types, formats, drivers, and minimizers, enabling effortless extension to emerging software. Key utilities include automated train-test splitting, coordinate perturbation for active learning, outlier-energy removal, Δ-learning data set generation, error-metric computation, and unit conversion. Through efficient NumPy-backed storage and system-level operations, dpdata achieves significant memory saving and inference speedups over configuration-by-configuration tools such as ASE. We also highlight practical impact, with dpdata used across published studies, for format conversion, data storage, coordinate perturbation, and utilization in other projects for data processing.

papers.title: Optimization of multi-echelon multi-product supply chains using discrete event simulation
papers.abstract: This study details the application of a novel multi-echelon, multi-product hybrid supply chain optimization framework known as the Optimizing Known Warehouses (OKW) framework, which consists of mathematical and computer simulation models, to analyze the effects of changes in inventory policies for products delivered by two (2) different case-study manufacturing supply chains. The methods used are the Bayesian optimization algorithm and linear programming to optimize inventory and routing in the supply chains. Furthermore, Arena software was used to develop a discrete event simulation model to compare the current and optimized scenarios of the supply chains. The results show that the optimization framework effectively reduces backorders and increases order fulfillment within the manufacturing supply chains analyzed, and can be easily applied to other Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) manufacturing supply chains. For the water bottling supply chain, the optimal inventory policies reduced backorders of the 50cl, 75cl, and 150cl bottled water products by 8.7%, 18.7%, and 34.7%, respectively. For the noodles manufacturing supply chain, backorders for the 70g, 100g, 120g, 180g, and 280g noodle products were reduced by 3.5%, 12%, 20.6%, 7.1%, and 11.9%, respectively. This study provides a procedure for inventory and routing optimization using Bayesian optimization and linear programming, respectively, and a Discrete Event Simulation model for analyzing various supply chain configurations.

papers.title: A sub-regional active learning-based hybrid network framework for remaining useful life prediction of offshore wind turbine gearboxes
papers.abstract: A sub-regional active learning-based hybrid network (SRAL-HNet) framework is proposed for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of offshore wind turbine gearboxes. First, a multi-scale sliding window strategy is employed to extract both short-term fluctuations and long-term degradation trends from the raw monitoring data. Then, the random forest is utilized for sensitivity features selection to eliminate redundant information. Subsequently, a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder and a fully connected (FC) regression head are combined to construct the BiLSTM-FC regression network. By combining health-index monotonicity analysis with percentile-based threshold segmentation, a sub-regional active learning method is developed to partition the sequence data into distinct regions. Consequently, the SRAL-HNet method is constructed for RUL prediction by integrating the sub-regional active learning model with the BiLSTM-FC regression network. To validate the feasibility and superiority of the proposed method, an offshore wind turbine SCADA dataset is used. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves accurate RUL predictions with a significant reduction in the number of samples required. Overall, the proposed framework is able to support offshore condition-based maintenance, risk-informed inspection planning, and life-extension decision-making in marine renewable energy systems.

papers.title: Dynamic response analysis and BO-CNN-SVM fault diagnosis of reversible solid oxide cells under dual-mode operation
papers.abstract: Reversible solid oxide cells (rSOC) are promising energy conversion devices due to their bidirectional operation capability, while fault diagnosis under dual-mode operation remains challenging. This study develops a data-driven fault diagnosis framework for rSOC systems by integrating convolutional neural network (CNN), radial basis function support vector machine (RBF-SVM), and Bayesian optimization (BO). Dynamic fault characteristics of fuel-side leakage, air-side leakage, and electrode interface delamination are investigated under both solid oxide fuel cell and solid oxide electrolysis cell modes using simulated operating data. The proposed Bayesian-optimized CNN-SVM model achieves a diagnostic accuracy of 97.55%, outperforming conventional SVM, CNN, and CNN-SVM models. The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively extracts transient fault features and provides accurate and reliable multi-fault diagnosis for reversible solid oxide cell systems.

papers.title: DELVING INTO THE LIVED EXPERIENCES OF SECONDARY SCIENCE TEACHERS ON THE USE OF THE 7E’S LESSON PLAN: A QUALITATIVE STUDY
papers.abstract: This phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of secondary science teachers in the Division of Tagum City as they implemented the 7Es lesson plan. Ten public school science teachers participated in the study through in-depth interviews and focus group discussions. Data were treated using thematic analysis. Findings revealed that teachers experienced cognitive exhaustion and instructional compression due to the demanding nature of the framework and time constraints. Despite these challenges, they emphasized that systematic planning enhanced student learning and improved instructional efficiency. To address difficulties, science teachers employed coping strategies such as consultation with master teachers and co-teachers, structural adaptations, pedagogical prioritization, and strategic, adaptive lesson planning to ensure operational readiness. Reported benefits include technology as a pedagogical tool for understanding scientific concepts, assessment as a responsive process for enhancing learning, and active learning as a pathway to scientific understanding. Teachers also established adaptation strategies such as flexible adjustments to 7E activities for diverse learners, guided support for independent student learning, and contextualized inquiry using local, real-life examples. Overall, the study highlights that while the 7Es lesson plan presents significant challenges, it also fosters meaningful learning outcomes.

papers.title: Low-Carbon Urban Morphology as a Configuration Problem: Empirically Constrained Bayesian Optimization at the Intra-Urban Scale
papers.abstract: Urban compactness and functional mixing are widely recognized as important carbon mitigation strategies. However, determining appropriate levels of compactness and functional mixing, and their potential carbon reductions, remains challenging due to nonlinear morphology–emission relationships and strong spatial dependence. This study develops a spatially explicit Bayesian optimization (SEBO) framework integrating spatial relationship analysis, nonlinear response-interval identification, and constrained configuration optimization. Using 4,347 grid cells in the Nanjing metropolitan region, spatial econometric models identify sector-specific morphology–emission associations and green-blue moderation effects. Tree-based machine learning then identifies responsive ranges for morphological adjustment, which constrain Bayesian optimization to explore lower-emission configurations and assess mitigation potential. Results reveal substantial sectoral differences in morphology–emission relationships and response intervals. Vertical intensity and functional mix are associated with transportation, residential, and power-related emissions, while horizontal density primarily relates to residential emissions. Optimizing vertical intensity yields average simulated reductions of 14.09%, 19.25%, and 5.75% in transportation, residential, and power-related emissions, respectively. However, mitigation potential varies with initial morphological and ecological conditions, with some scenarios yielding higher predicted emissions. These findings support spatially differentiated, context-specific urban morphology optimization rather than universal compactness targets.

papers.title: Flashcard creation and use in a histology lecture course: A survey-based case study.
papers.abstract: Histology, like many basic science subjects requires mastery of terminology, visual structures, and integration of these things to describe functional relationships, making effective study strategies essential for student success. Flashcards are widely used to support retrieval practice and spaced repetition, but students can struggle to develop deeper understanding beyond surface memorization. The relatively recent integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into mainstream higher education exposes new opportunities to enhance active learning strategies. This case study assesses the extent to which flashcards are being used by students in a histology lecture class, and explores the role that AI plays. Data were collected through two voluntary online surveys that included questions asking for multiple-choice responses and short written responses. The subjective and quantitative comparisons together with students’ self-reflection statements prompted classroom discussions about intentional flashcard design and use, and the broader applicability of course-specific study strategies.

papers.title: Investigation of the surface oxidation behavior of iron-based alloys using recoilless nuclear gamma resonance
papers.abstract: The recoilless nuclear gamma resonance method, also known as Mössbauer spectroscopy, is a non-destructive method of studying the solid state. This technique can be used to determine the phase composition, local atomic environments, magnetic properties, and the nature of chemical bonds. The experiment requires an iron-containing material to observe the effect of resonant absorption of gamma quanta. One advantage of Mössbauer spectroscopy is that it enables the study of materials both in thin surface layers and in bulk. Mössbauer spectroscopy makes it possible to register different decay products of an excited nucleus. Conversion electron Mössbauer spectroscopy (CEMS) provides information on the structure of materials at a depth of 0.3 𝜇m. On the contrary, Conversion X-ray Mössbauer spectroscopy (CXMS) has a probing depth of around 10 𝜇m. This study examined the impact of high-temperature treatment on the formation of oxide layers in steels and iron-based alloys used in additive manufacturing. The samples studied were produced by selective laser melting (SLM) of austenitic 316L stainless steel and 1.2709 maraging steel powder. Following 3D printing, the surface of the material was subjected to mechanical polishing and sandblasting, after which it was thermally annealed in air at a temperature ranging from 500 to 1000 °C. The surface of samples was studied using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy dispersion analysis (EDS), X-ray diffraction (XRD) and grazing incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD), in conjunction with the Mössbauer spectroscopy method. Following exposure to temperature, an austenitic iron phase (𝛾-Fe) is present throughout the bulk of 316L stainless steel. The CXMS singlet corresponding to the 𝛾-phase exhibits slight quadrupole splitting indicating the presence of alloying element atoms in the FCC lattice. The CEMS method revealed phase transformations 𝛾→𝛼 in a thin surface layer measuring around 0.2-0.3 𝜇m. The presence of an oxide phase containing iron was also indicated by the detection of a Fe3+ doublet. An increase in the annealing temperature and exposure time of the samples in the laboratory furnace resulted in an increase in oxide scale, which exhibited an inhomogeneous structure. A combination of MS and other methods (XRD, EDS) revealed that the surface of 316L stainless steel is covered with trigonal mixed oxides (Fe-Cr)₂O₃ and Mn-rich oxides Mn₂(Fe-Cr)O₄ after temperature impact. For 1.2709 maraging steel, the method of surface treatment affects the oxidation process. Using the CEMS and GIXRD methods, it was found that surface treatment involving mechanical polishing and heating leads to the formation of 𝛼-Fe2O3, whereas 𝛾-Fe2O3 forms on surfaces treated with sandblasting. GIXRD also revealed that the surface of the 1.2709 maraging steel was inhomogeneous at different incident angles. CEMS showed that at a depth of approximately 0.2 𝜇m the sandblasted and heated (at 500 °C for 2 hours) surface contains of the 𝛾-Fe2O3 of and 𝛼-Fe2O3. According to CEMS, the polished and heated (at 500 °C for 2 hours) surface contains of retained austenite and 𝛼-Fe2O3.

papers.title: Investigation of the surface behavior of 1.2709 maraging steel produced by SLM following post-processing treatment. Application of Mössbauer spectroscopy to materials used in additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: Maraging steel is a high-strength material with enhanced mechanical properties. Mössbauer spectroscopy (MS), also known as recoilless nuclear gamma resonance, can be used to study the surface and bulk of a material. Conversion X-ray Mössbauer spectroscopy (CXMS) and conversion electron Mössbauer spectroscopy (CEMS) provide information about the structure of materials at different depths: 10 µm and 0.3 µm, respectively. This method can reveal information about the inhomogeneity of the material's surface layer. In this research, the study samples were made from 1.2709 maraging steel metal powder using selective laser melting (SLM). The initial samples were in the shape of a cylinder with 25 mm diameter and 5 mm height. After 3D printing, the surface of the studied samples was subjected to a post-production treatment process. The samples were studied under the following conditions: after sandblasting; after sandblasting and annealing at 500 °C in air, after polishing; and after polishing and annealing at 500 °C in air. Studies of the phase composition and phase transformations of 1.2709 maraging steel have revealed the relation between surface treatment methods and phase distribution. A detailed investigation of the surface of the sample revealed that the initial sandblasted and polished samples contained martensite and retained austenite phases. The phase composition in the surface layer is also affected by the surface treatment method. While the polished sample showed only the martensitic phase, sandblasting preserved both the austenitic and martensitic phases. The samples exposed to temperature also show the presence of iron oxide (α-Fe2O3) at a depth of around 10 μm. Studies of the thin surface layer at depth between 0.1 and 0.4 μm have revealed that the surface is inhomogeneous. A polished surface tends to create the α-Fe2O3 oxide when exposed to temperature, whereas a sandblasted surface is covered with γ-Fe2O3.

papers.title: Investigation of process parameters of laser powder bed fusion to manufacture crack-free M2 high-speed steel
papers.abstract: This study detailed the optimisation of process parameters for the laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) additive manufacturing process to produce crack-free, high-density M2 high-speed steel alloy. The high carbon content of this steel increases its susceptibility to cracking under the steep thermal gradients of the LPBF process. The work identifies optimised processing parameters for manufacturing defect-free M2 high-speed steel with minimal residual stress. A matrix of samples was built by varying laser power and scan speed, under 180°C platform heating. It was found that there are three distinct sample behaviours, categorised by volumetric energy density (VED): build failure at high energy density, macro-cracking at intermediate energy density and sound but porous structures at low energy density. X-ray diffraction analysis of cracked samples revealed phase transformations with varying VED, suggesting that the thermal gradient played a significant role in crack formation. While analysing the set of samples without visible macro-cracking, a critical VED of 27 J/mm 3 was identified, resulting in a crack-free sample when using a relatively low power (225 W) and low speed (1000 mm/s) combination, which reduces thermal stress. Using this optimal baseline, the process was further refined by adjusting the laser hatch distance. Decreasing the hatch distance from 140 µm to 120 µm successfully minimised internal porosity by promoting ideal melt pool overlap. The optimised process yielded fully dense, crack-free parts with a relative density of 99.38% (8.11 g.cm −3 ) and an as-built hardness of 643 HV0.5.

papers.title: Operator-Splitting Error Bounds for Physics-Informed Neural Emulation of Coupled Land–Atmosphere Fluxes Under Diurnal Forcing: Convergence Guarantees and Drought-Onset Advisory Reliability
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) that emulate coupled land–atmosphere fluxes must reconcile two disparate time scales: the stiff, sub-hourly relaxation of the surface energy balance and the slow, multi-day accumulation of moisture deficits that underpins drought-onset advisories. Operator splitting offers a principled route to this reconciliation, but its interaction with neural-network approximation error has not been bounded in a form usable by advisory systems. the present analysis derives a posteriori error bounds for a Lie–Trotter splitting of the coupled surface energy and moisture budget equations when each sub-step is emulated by a physics-informed network. The analysis separates splitting error, network approximation error and accumulated forcing error, and shows that the drought-onset advisory reliability is governed by the accumulated moisture residual rather than by instantaneous flux accuracy. The bounds are stated as explicit inequalities involving the Lipschitz constants of the flux parameterisations and the network training residual, and they yield a certified advisory horizon beyond which a drought-onset warning cannot be trusted. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-derived temperature record for Lagos, Nigeria (NASA POWER MERRA-2, 2000–2023, 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C, standard deviation 0.943 °C, warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which supplies the diurnal-forcing envelope within which the bounds are evaluated. The contribution is a certified reliability criterion for drought-onset advisories built on split PINN emulators, together with the conditions under which that criterion can be tightened by refining the moisture sub-step alone.

papers.title: D3.1 Specification requirements for experimental infrastructures
papers.abstract: This deliverable presents the outcomes of Task 3.4 of the ENDURANCE project, which aims to identify requirements for large-scale experimental and qualification infrastructures supporting the development, safety assessment and licensing of molten salt reactors (MSRs) in Europe. The report reviews the experimental development programmes of two industrial partners, Saltfoss and Thorizon, and analyses their responses to a questionnaire on large-scale testing needs. Topics include the scaling of safety-relevant physical phenomena, material and component qualification, criticality experiments, fuel lifecycle activities, integrated-effects testing, decommissioning and severe-accident testing. The analysis identifies areas of agreement, including the importance of representative experimental conditions for natural circulation, salt freezing and remelting, multiphase flow, corrosion, and fission-product transport, while recognising differences arising from individual reactor concepts. The deliverable recommends a coordinated European approach based on a portfolio of complementary experimental infrastructures: large-scale facilities for phenomena that are difficult to scale down, shared capabilities for materials and component qualification, and facilities supporting fuel-related activities. It emphasises flexible test platforms, robust instrumentation, data quality and uncertainty quantification to increase the relevance of experimental evidence for model validation and licensing. As the assessment is based on two industrial responses, the findings represent an initial basis for further consultation and infrastructure planning.

papers.title: Sequential Decision Under Partial Observability for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Irrigation Scheduling Under Unmodeled Soil Dynamics: A Computer Regret-Bound Comparison
papers.abstract: Irrigation scheduling under partial observability is formalised as a finite-horizon partially observable Markov decision process in which the soil-moisture transition kernel is not known to the controller. Four candidate policies are compared: certainty-equivalent model predictive control, a point-based value iteration approximation, a Thompson-sampling bandit, and a sliding-window online learner. The comparison is analytical rather than empirical: for each policy a regret bound is derived as a function of the observation horizon, the size of the unmodeled dynamics class, and the number of irrigation decisions per season. The central result is that the regret of certainty-equivalent control grows linearly in the horizon whenever the unmodeled transition error is nonzero, whereas the online learner attains sublinear regret of order the square root of the horizon under a bounded-elasticity assumption on the soil-moisture response. The bound gap is quantified for a reference parameterisation with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, and the cluster count required for eighty per cent power at a five percentage-point effect is reported as 54. The contribution is a decision-theoretic account of when partial observability is tolerable in irrigation scheduling and when it forces exploration, together with a reproducible regret-bound template that can be instantiated for any bounded soil-moisture model class.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network Surrogates for Agriculture Drainage Design Under Uncertain Soil Permeability: A Computer Calibration-Reliability Evaluation
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) promise fast surrogates for the Richards equation in agricultural drainage design, but their reliability under uncertain soil permeability is rarely quantified. The framework separates epistemic calibration error from aleatoric permeability uncertainty and derives a reliability bound on the surrogate's predicted water-table drawdown. A formal analysis establishes conditions under which the PINN residual loss bounds the expected design error, and a variance decomposition identifies the intraclass correlation of the permeability field as the dominant driver of surrogate reliability. The analysis is theoretical and methodological: no observational data are used or claimed. The framework is operationalised through a design-based evaluation that characterises the operating characteristics of a before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64), with power estimated across 2000 design cells. The results indicate that 54 clusters are required for 80% power at a 5 percentage-point effect, and that the intraclass correlation of 0.64 inflates the minimum detectable effect substantially at small cluster counts. The contribution is a reliability-aware calibration protocol that lets drainage engineers decide when a PINN surrogate is trustworthy enough to replace a numerical solver in design loops.

papers.abstract: Marine construction materials exposed to harsh ocean conditions gradually degrade as a result of series of processes, such as the effects of chloride-driven corrosive processes, temperature cycling, salinity, dissolved oxygen content, pH, hydrodynamic flow, mechanical loadings, creating serious problems related to sustainable marine infrastructure. In this research, Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) is proposed for prediction of marine materials degradation under various ocean conditions. Marine structural steel samples were subjected to controlled seawater conditions and analyzed using Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Electron Dispersive X-Ray Spectroscopy (EDS) in order to determine degradation indicators. Features were incorporated with environment parameters and material characteristics to create multi-physical feature matrix. PINN incorporates governing physical laws through the physics-based optimization method. Experimental validation produced R2 = 0.956, RMSE = 0.083 mm, MAE = 0.061 mm which proves that degradation of marine engineering constructions can be predicted with high level of accuracy, reliability, and validity.

papers.title: Differentiable control of laser–plasma experiments with conditional diffusion models
papers.abstract: Abstract Tuning a laser--wakefield accelerator to a desired electron energy spectrum is normally done by scanning the machine one setting at a time, which consumes scarce beam time and expert attention. We address the inverse problem directly, recovering the experimental settings that produce a target spectrum. To do so we train a conditional diffusion model, built on the Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Models (EDM) framework, on measured electron spectra from the ALFA beamline, conditioned on laser energy, gas-jet backing pressure, and gas-valve opening time. Because EDM samples by integrating a probability-flow ordinary differential equation, the map from settings to spectrum is differentiable end to end, and the settings themselves can be treated as free variables and optimized by backpropagation through the sampler. We propose and evaluate a three-stage strategy, \mbox{BO $\to$ L-BFGS $\to$ RAdam}, in which Bayesian optimization provides a global warm start across flat regions, L-BFGS exploits local curvature, and a final stochastic phase relaxes the solution away from sharp, bin-aligned minima. Against seven alternative single- and multi-stage strategies, this ordering recovers the target settings with the lowest mean squared error. We position this as a tool for differentiable inverse design in experiment planning, complementary to particle-in-cell simulation rather than a substitute for it.

papers.title: Enhanced Fault Ride-Through of Grid-Connected PV Systems Using PIR-MPC-Controlled Supercapacitor Energy Storage
papers.abstract: Abstract Grid-connected solar photovoltaic (GSPV) systems experience prominent double-frequency oscillations in the DC-link voltage, real and reactive power during asymmetrical grid fault scenarios, which can severely affect low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) capability. This paper proposes a combined control strategy based on an optimized supercapacitor energy storage system (SCESS) and negative-sequence reactive current injection for improving the LVRT capability of GSPV systems under an extensive range of short circuit ratio (SCR) conditions. A multi-objective optimization method is formulated to simultaneously minimize DC-link voltage ripple, real and reactive power oscillations, and SCESS energy requirements. A proportionalintegral-resonant (PIR) controller is employed for DC-link voltage regulation, while finite control set based model predictive control (FCS-MPC) is implemented to achieve fast and accurate current tracking. The PIR and MPC gains, together with the negative-sequence reactive current contributing factor, are optimally determined within the proposed methodology. A dual second-order generalized integrator phase-locked loop (DSOGI-PLL) is incorporated for offering better synchronization under unbalanced and distorted grid conditions. Unlike conventional strategies based on braking choppers (BC) and positive-sequenceprioritized reactive current injection, the proposed approach coordinates SCESS power exchange with optimal negative-sequence current compensation, thereby improving the mitigation of double-frequency oscillations of the DC-link voltage, real and reactive power during severe asymmetrical fault scenarios. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is evaluated under balanced and unbalanced faults and different SCR conditions. Simulation results and comparative analysis demonstrate significant reductions of the double frequency oscillations in the DC-link voltage, real and reactive power injections while maintaining the required LVRT response and limiting the SCESS energy requirement. The proposed multi-objective coordinated control strategy therefore provides an effective solution for robust grid integration of GSPV systems under adverse grid conditions.

papers.title: Budgeted Active Learning for Agriculture Soil Fertility Mapping Under Costly Laboratory Assays: An Artificial Intelligence Information-Gain Regret Bound
papers.abstract: Soil fertility mapping in smallholder agriculture is constrained by the cost of laboratory assays, which limits the number of plots that can be sampled and therefore the accuracy of the resulting maps. The framework is analysed through an information-gain regret bound that decomposes the excess risk of the learned map into an approximation term, a noise term and an information term governed by the mutual information between selected plots and the fertility field. The bound is derived under a Gaussian process prior over the fertility field and a submodular information-gain objective, and it is shown that greedy selection attains a constant-factor approximation to the optimal information gain, which yields a regret bound that scales with the square root of the budget rather than with the number of candidate plots. The analysis is complemented by a design-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator used to assess mapping accuracy, with a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.64; power was estimated across 2000 design cells and 52 clusters were required for a 5 percentage point effect at 80% power. The results clarify when active selection is worth its computational and logistical cost and when uniform sampling is preferable.

papers.title: Full Waveform Inversion via Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning for CO2 Plume Detection
papers.abstract: This study presents a probabilistic deep learning framework developed for full waveform inversion (FWI) to detect and characterise subsurface velocity anomalies induced by stored CO2. Three convolutional neural network architectures—LinkNet, UNet, and a feature pyramid network (FPN)—were trained and evaluated on the Kimberlina CO2 synthetic dataset from the OpenFWI repository, which simulates CO2 injection scenarios within stratified reservoirs. The FPN architecture with an SE-ResNet50 backbone achieved the best performance (R2=0.9386, MSE=3.1676×10−4, MAE=4.5249×10−3). Uncertainty quantification was performed using variational inference with the Flipout estimator, which enables the separation of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. The predicted velocity models accurately reconstruct the background stratigraphy and the low-velocity anomaly associated with the CO2 plume. The aleatoric uncertainty remains at around 101 m/s and is spatially localised to delineate the geometry of the low-velocity zone. In contrast, the epistemic uncertainty is several orders of magnitude smaller, at around 10−3 m/s, and increases specifically over the lowest-velocity region of the anomaly. This structured distribution indicates where the velocity reconstruction is least reliable. Calibration substantially reduced the overall miscalibration area, decreasing the magnitude of the aleatoric component while slightly increasing that of the epistemic uncertainty over the CO2 plume anomaly, although the spatial structure of both components remained unchanged. This uncertainty decomposition and calibration help to distinguish between data noise and model limitations. It provides direct information for designing acquisitions and assessing risks, which is an area that is not widely covered in the current literature.

papers.title: Active-Learning Evaluation for Computer Agriculture Pest-Surveillance Classifiers Under Budget-Constrained Scouting: An Artificial Intelligence Query-Selection Bound for Detection Efficiency
papers.abstract: Active learning promises to reduce the annotation cost of pest-surveillance classifiers by selecting only the most informative field queries, yet the evaluation of query-selection strategies under realistic scouting budgets remains informal, and reported gains are rarely tied to a formal bound on detection efficiency. No observational data are used or claimed: the analysis characterises the operating characteristics of the design under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5 and intraclass correlation = 0.64, across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The bound decomposes detection efficiency into an informativeness term and a coverage term, and it predicts that the marginal value of an additional query falls as the intraclass correlation rises. The design study indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that power curves, minimum detectable effect curves and residual diagnostics behave as the bound anticipates. The contribution is a formal, falsifiable criterion for evaluating active-learning query selection in agricultural pest surveillance, together with a design-level statement of the cluster counts at which the criterion becomes informative.

papers.title: An interpretable DM-PINN for retrieving mangrove canopy carbon, nitrogen, and potassium contents using Sentinel-2 and SDGSAT-1 observations along China's southeastern coast
papers.abstract: Mangroves are among the most important blue carbon ecosystems, contributing substantially to global carbon sequestration and biodiversity conservation. Canopy carbon (CCC), nitrogen (CNC), and potassium (CKC) contents provide critical indicators of nutrient cycling, ecosystem functioning, and ecological health. However, the structural complexity and strong spatial heterogeneity of mangroves present major obstacles to understanding the spectral response mechanisms and achieving reliable large-scale retrieval of these biochemical parameters. To address these limitations, we developed an interpretable retrieval framework that integrates causal analysis with physical constraints for reliable estimation of mangrove biochemical parameters. First, we proposed a Multi-Channel Chatterjee-Enhanced Correlation Spectrum Analysis (MC-ξ-CS) method that integrates causal discovery to systematically identify spectral bands causally associated with CCC, CNC, and CKC. For large-scale retrieval of mangrove canopy parameters, the identified causal relationships were transferred to satellite observations through a Global Angle-Divergence Spectral Transfer (GADT) framework, yielding robust estimation (R2 = 0.511–0.669). Subsequently, a Dual-Mechanism Guided Physics-Informed Neural Network (DM-PINN) was developed to synergistically integrate causal analysis and physical constraints, achieving robust retrieval performance (R2 = 0.604–0.83) for three representative mangrove species and enhancing the physical interpretability of the results. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first comprehensive large-scale retrieval of key mangrove biochemical parameters along the southeastern coast of China, revealing CCC values of 409.18–566.89 g/kg (C/N = 9.77–14.21), CNC values of 14.38–74.9 g/kg (N/K = 1.99–3.86), and CKC values of 4.78–19.67 g/kg (C/K = 28.22–37.67). Distinct inter-provincial spatial patterns were observed: CNC and CKC exhibited similar gradients, increasing from landward to seaward regions, whereas CCC displayed an opposite spatial distribution pattern with lower values in coastal regions. Moreover, CCC was strongly positively correlated with CNC, while CKC showed negative correlations with both parameters. Collectively, this study established a novel theoretical and methodological framework for elucidating the spectral response mechanisms of mangrove biochemical parameters, offering critical scientific support for large-scale mangrove degradation monitoring, ecological restoration assessment, and biodiversity conservation.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Inference for Computer Agriculture Crop-Disease Forecasting Under Scarce Labeled Field Imagery: An Artificial Intelligence Active-Sampling Generalization Bound
papers.abstract: Crop-disease forecasting from field imagery is constrained less by model capacity than by the cost of acquiring labelled examples, and active learning is the standard remedy. The bound is derived under a Tsybakov margin condition and a disagreement-coefficient assumption, and it yields an explicit label-complexity rate that is then embedded in a design analysis. The design analysis used a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5 and intraclass correlation = 0.64, and estimated power across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. Power rose with cluster count and effect size, and 56 clusters were required for 80% power at a 5-percentage-point effect. The bound and the design analysis together specify the conditions under which an active-sampling claim is identifiable from a field trial, and they identify the cluster count at which the claim becomes testable.

papers.title: Benchmarking Evaluation of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Computer Agriculture Soil-Nitrogen Transport Under Sparse Lysimeter Calibration: An Artificial Intelligence Mass-Balance Violation Bound for Fertilizer Leaching Regulation
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) promise to embed mass-conservation laws into data-driven soil-nitrogen transport models, yet the reliability of that promise under sparse lysimeter calibration is unknown. The framework is evaluated through a replication-based design study of the before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64), with power estimated across 2000 design cells at cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points.54 clusters are required for 80% power at a 5-percentage-point effect, and it formalises the PINN mass-balance violation as a bounded functional of the calibration residual. The derived bound converts a network's training residual into a worst-case leaching-load error, providing regulators with an auditable threshold rather than a point prediction. The contribution is a benchmark protocol and a violation bound that together make PINN-based nitrogen models accountable to the mass-balance requirement that fertilizer regulation presupposes.

papers.title: Using the Purpose Anchored Team (PAT™) Framework to Diagnose Team Performance Problems: An Executive-Team Coaching Case
papers.abstract: Team performance problems may appear as conflict, slow decisions, repeated escalation or weak accountability, yet these symptoms may be generated by conditions at systemic levels. This paper introduces the Purpose Anchored Team (PAT™) Framework as a theory-informed diagnostic architecture for team performance. PAT™ does not propose another list of team-effectiveness factors. Instead, it uses stakeholder-derived team purpose as an organising criterion for locating performance problems within the team, within the organisation or in changing ecosystem demands. A 10-month executive-team coaching case illustrates the diagnostic sequence from presenting symptoms to problem formulation informed by multiple case data sources and established theory, intervention locus and operating changes. Data included interviews, coaching observations, organisational documents, decision records, pulse measures, stakeholder feedback and practitioner notes. PAT™ subsequently informed interventions in purpose clarification, decision architecture, organisational reinforcement and active learning routines. Descriptive changes are reported without claiming causal effectiveness or empirical validation of the framework.

papers.title: Motion Retargeting with Spatiotemporal Preferences for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Human motion retargeting bridges the embodiment gap between humans and humanoid robots by converting human demonstrations into reference trajectories for whole-body control and loco-manipulation. For object-interaction tasks, successful execution depends on accurately preserving body--object relations at critical stages. However, uniform per-frame iteration budgets do not account for these localized accuracy requirements, limiting the computational efficiency of retargeting. To address this limitation, we present Spatiotemporal Retargeting (STR), which uses keyframes and key body parts to allocate optimization effort. Specifically, a vision-language model selects relevant motion signals and body parts, and keyframes are identified from changes in the selected signals. Based on these selections, STR assigns additional solver iterations to keyframes and higher interaction weights to the selected parts. To further improve contact fidelity, we introduce Mechanics-Aware Contact Anchoring (MCA) to refine object-surface contact positions using an approximate object-wrench model while retaining the selected surface directions. Building on the resulting references, we develop Spatiotemporal Reinforcement Learning (STRL), which combines adaptive key-stage sampling with a contact reward based on target proximity and object contact forces for downstream control. Simulation experiments on a Unitree G1 and real-world experiments on a Unitree R1 demonstrate that STR improves geometric contact coverage and continuity at lower computational cost, while the resulting references improve downstream task completion across diverse object-interaction motions.

papers.title: Learning to Incentivise: Using Reinforcement Learning for Sustainable Urban Mobility
papers.abstract: Traffic management has traditionally focused on toll-based and road pricing solutions. However, road pricing often raises concerns about accessibility and public dissatisfaction, leading to its prohibition in some places, such as Finland. This study optimises the dynamic allocation of incentives to drivers, encouraging them to reroute onto alternative (potentially longer) paths to achieve greater societal benefit, reduced total travel time (TTT) and total emissions in the transportation network, contributing to sustainable urban mobility. We employ a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach to dynamically assign incentives to drivers to reduce both TTT and emissions, with travel times estimated using traffic simulation software. We demonstrate that, with an unlimited budget and an objective of minimising travel time, the incentive scheme reduces TTT by 16%, compared to the dynamic User-Equilibrium (UE) with a budget equivalent to about 11% of the UE total time. When the goal is to minimise emissions, a 9% reduction in CO2 emissions is observed under an unlimited budget. We demonstrate a critical trade-off: minimising TTT leads to an increase in emissions, while prioritising emission reductions raises TTT. However, with the right combination of weights in the multi-objective function, both TTT and total emissions are improved beyond the baseline.
