papers.title: AcoustiPrint: Physics-Guided Neural Design of Manufacturable Acoustic Structures
papers.abstract: Recent work in additive manufacturing and neural inverse design enables the creation of complex three-dimensional structures to manipulate physical fields, yet these designs must also adhere to discrete, non-differentiable fabrication constraints. Current methods limit the design space by imposing differentiable soft manufacturability loss penalties, or by fixing structures through post-processing, causing a discrepancy between the geometry optimized by the physics model and the final fabricated result. Thus, we present AcoustiPrint, a physics-informed neural architecture for constrained inverse design that represents three-dimensional geometries with an implicit neural representation (INR) and passes each candidate through a printability operator before evaluating its final response. The printability operator executes layer-wise self-support, discrete material selection, and whole-body connectivity, assuring fabrication feasibility. To allow for backpropagation through the discrete non-differentiable operations, we use surrogate gradients for the backward pass and a self-supervised printability objective that progressively drives the INR toward a valid design domain. We demonstrate AcoustiPrint for personalized transcranial focused ultrasound, where inter-patient differences in acoustic properties and head geometry deform wave propagation and requires patient-specific acoustic focusing. AcoustiPrint jointly optimizes three-dimensional geometry and material composition through differentiable wave physics while ensuring manufacturability. Experiments show manufacturable acoustic structures with enhanced focal accuracy and over density-based and phase-based baselines, demonstrating a generalized methodology for neural design through non-differentiable manufacturing constraints and differentiable physics.

papers.title: Microstructural Generative Inverse Models for Additive Manufacturing Digital Twins
papers.abstract: Metal additive manufacturing (AM) offers substantial advantages to the fabrication of complex structural components, but its widespread adoption is slowed due to complexities in the process-structure-property relations which is the cause for uncertainty and drives risk. Accurately quantifying these complex relations solely via experimental workflows is time consuming and costly. Integrated computational materials and engineering (ICME) frameworks address this challenge by leveraging advanced computational tools, such as crystal plasticity finite element models (CPFEM), to predict critical mechanical properties directly from microstructural data. However, these frameworks require a large datasets that are often difficult to obtain, and their predictive accuracy depends on the availability of realistic AM microstructure representations. Generative deep learning models are a promising approach towards synthesizing AM microstructures which contain complex morphological and crystallographic features. Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs), in particular, show a strong potential to capture the inherent complexities of AM structures. In this work, we demonstrate that DDPMs can reliably synthesize digital-twin orientation-imaging micrographs, and we support this claim with quantitative evidence of the fidelity of the generated samples. Additionally, we establish a classifier-free guidance framework for solving complex inverse problems such as property-to-structure and process-to-structure mappings, and we showcase a potential application on a qualification-relevant uncertainty quantification problem. Our work highlights the potential of AI-based generative modeling as a key component of computational frameworks for accelerating AM materials qualification and certification.

papers.title: Dynamic Active Fleet Sizing of Heterogeneous UAV Relays for Post-Disaster Communication Networks
papers.abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems are increasingly used to provide temporary connectivity when ground communication infrastructure is damaged by disasters such as hurricanes and wildfires. However, the amount of aerial support required changes as ground networks recover and communication demand evolves. We focus on dynamically adjusting the number and allocation of actively deployed UAVs within a fixed available fleet. We develop a model predictive control (MPC) framework for dynamic fleet sizing of heterogeneous UAV relays during post-disaster communication recovery. The framework accounts for communication demand, ground network recovery, heterogeneous UAV operation, UAV energy availability, and backhaul capacity, which limits how much relayed traffic can be transmitted to the external communication network. The resulting formulation is a convex quadratic program that supports efficient online fleet sizing and deployment decisions. We evaluate the framework using seven historical disaster recovery case studies based on Federal Communications Commission reports, together with four backhaul scenarios and sensitivity analyses. Results show that required active UAV fleet size varies considerably throughout recovery, while backhaul capacity and fleet composition affect communication performance, highlighting the value of adapting active fleet size over time.

papers.title: Spectral Uncertainty Decomposition for Sparse Bayesian Learning
papers.abstract: Estimating distributed neural sources from M/EEG measurements is an ill-posed inverse problem where principled uncertainty quantification remains challenging. The usual conditional Gaussian posterior covariance does not explicitly distinguish uncertainty along likelihood-visible source directions from uncertainty that is invisible to the measurements. We propose a spectral framework based on the singular value structure of the prior-preconditioned forward operator, which provides an exact, interpretable decomposition of the posterior covariance into data-informed and indeterminacy epistemic components. This formulation identifies uncertainty contributions that are reducible by better measurements from those that are fundamentally irreducible by sensing geometry. We further derive an equivalent subtractive decomposition that expresses the prior covariance as the sum of posterior and data-driven reduction terms, enabling precise accounting of uncertainty reduction through Bayesian learning. Together, these complementary representations offer both theoretical insight and practical tools for interpretable uncertainty quantification in M/EEG source imaging for linear-Gaussian Bayesian inverse solvers where the posterior covariance is available in closed form.

papers.title: Machine Learning Surrogate Modeling for Finite-Element Biomechanical Prediction and Design Screening in Implant-Supported Prostheses
papers.abstract: Finite-element analysis (FEA) is a widely used computational method for predicting the biomechanical response of implant-supported prostheses, but its computational cost limits its use in large-scale parametric exploration or chairside decision support. This study evaluated whether supervised machine learning models trained on finite-element simulations can act as accurate, near-instantaneous surrogates, whether their predictions are driven by physically plausible input variables, and whether their residual error is small enough to preserve the verdict of a downstream, illustrative design-screening protocol. A finite-element dataset was generated for 100 independently meshed and solved parent configurations of a fixed, four-implant (“All-on-4”-type) implant-supported prosthesis, varying seven geometry-level input variables (bone quality, bar material, implant diameter and length, implant tilt angle, cantilever length, and occlusal load angle) using a custom three-dimensional finite-element solver implemented in Python; each parent solution was then linearly scaled to 71 occlusal-load magnitudes, yielding a 7100-row modeling dataset with four biomechanical outputs per row: 95th-percentile (P95) cortical bone von Mises stress, P95 trabecular bone von Mises stress, maximum prosthesis displacement, and P95 bone principal strain. All 100 parent simulations converged and passed internal quality-control checks on solver residuals and force-balance equilibrium. Because rows sharing a parent geometry are not statistically independent, all partitioning and cross-validation were performed at the geometry level: 20 geometries (1420 rows) were held out a priori as a fixed test set, and the remaining 80 geometries (5680 rows) formed a development pool on which Random Forest, XGBoost, and support-vector regression (SVR) models were compared using grouped cross-validation GroupKFold keyed on parent geometry, 5 folds × 5 repeats, 25 matched folds), with model selection performed independently for each output based on the lowest mean cross-validated RMSE. This yielded a different winning model per output rather than a single globally best algorithm: target-scaled SVR for both P95 cortical stress (1.919±0.501 MPa) and P95 trabecular stress (0.168±0.039 MPa), Random Forest for maximum displacement (0.190±0.079 mm), and XGBoost for P95 principal strain (166.3±77.8 με). Friedman and Holm-corrected pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests corroborated that this ranking was consistent across resampled folds, but the more practically relevant evidence is the magnitude of the differences themselves, which is reported primarily as percentage RMSE reduction and matched-pairs rank-biserial effect size: 14.5% (cortical stress), 1.5% (trabecular stress, a practically negligible difference), 9.4% (displacement), and 15.0% (principal strain). Each selected model was refit on the full 80-geometry development pool and evaluated once, without further tuning, on the fixed 20-geometry (1420-row) test set. On this held-out test set, the selected models achieved coefficients of determination (R2) of 0.985 (95% bootstrap CI 0.976 to 0.993) for cortical stress, 0.968 (0.946 to 0.982) for trabecular stress, 0.986 (0.977 to 0.993) for maximum displacement, and 0.931 (0.883 to 0.980) for principal strain, with mean absolute percentage errors between 7.99% and 14.88%. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis of the actual selected model for each output (TreeExplainer for Random Forest and XGBoost; KernelExplainer for SVR) showed that occlusal load magnitude was the dominant driver of both stress outputs and of principal strain (39 to 45% of attributed importance), bone quality contributed materially to trabecular stress and strain (19% and 31%, respectively), and bar material was the leading driver of maximum displacement (50%), whereas implant diameter and tilt angle together contributed well under 10% of attributed importance for every output. Applying an illustrative biomechanical design-screening protocol (combining Frost’s mechanostat strain zones with Misch bone-quality-adjusted safety margins, with structural veto thresholds calibrated on the 80-geometry development pool only) independently to the true and surrogate-predicted outputs of all 1420 held-out test rows yielded an identical screening flag in 1301 rows (91.6%), with discordant rows concentrated close to a decision-zone boundary (89.9% of discordances within 20% of the boundary) rather than distributed uniformly across the design space, and this agreement rate was stable (91.5 to 92.3%) across alternative Misch discount-factor magnitudes. These results indicate that, within the sampled design space of this parametric finite-element model, output-specific machine learning surrogates can reproduce its biomechanical outputs with good numerical accuracy and physically interpretable feature attributions at a fraction of the computational cost, supporting their exploratory use as surrogate models for rapid design screening rather than as a substitute for clinical judgment or experimental validation.

papers.title: Reliability Analysis of Uncertain Correlation During the Construction Period of a Cantilevered Arch Considering Temperature Effects
papers.abstract: To investigate the influence of temperature effects on the reliability of cantilever-cast arch bridges during construction, and to comprehensively account for uncertain correlations among multiple variables, this paper proposes a time-varying reliability analysis framework for cantilever-cast reinforced concrete arch bridges during construction, with explicit consideration of temperature effects and uncertain correlations among multiple random variables. The framework integrates Copula functions with Bayesian Dynamic Models (BDMs) to overcome two key limitations of conventional reliability approaches: the common assumption of variable independence and the inability to dynamically update reliability estimates using field monitoring data. The Gaussian Copula is adopted to characterize the nonlinear dependence structures among construction-stage variables—including cable forces, material properties, and ambient temperature—while the AR(1)-based BDM enables recursive state prediction and real-time reliability updating. To ensure computational tractability for large-scale finite element models, an XGBoost surrogate model (R2 = 0.97, RMSE = 0.76 MPa), selected through systematic comparison against six alternative methods, is coupled with an improved Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) optimization algorithm for efficient computation of component and system reliability indices. The proposed framework is validated through three independent exercises: Monte Carlo simulation using the surrogate model with 106 samples (relative errors < 3.2%), comparison with FORM and independent-assumption approaches, and an analytical benchmark (relative error 1.2%). Application to the Shatuo Bridge—a 240 m span reinforced concrete deck arch bridge constructed by the cantilever casting method—demonstrates that temperature effects reduce the arch rib stress reliability index from β = 4.25 under ideal conditions to β = 3.98 under actual construction conditions, a reduction of approximately 6.3%. The system reliability index, accounting for failure-mode correlations via the Gaussian Copula, is β = 3.921, which is lower than the independent-failure prediction (β = 4.11) but still exceeds the target reliability of 3.5 specified in Chinese code JTG 2120-2020. Quantification of epistemic uncertainties—surrogate-model error (1.1%), model-form uncertainty (4.2%), and parameter-estimation uncertainty (1.5%)—yields a reliability index range of β = 3.81–3.97, confirming the robustness of the safety assessment. Global sensitivity analysis using Sobol indices identifies the arch rib elastic modulus (38% variance contribution), unit weight (21%), cable forces (15% combined), temperature (12%), and thermal expansion coefficient (8%) as the dominant factors governing structural safety. The proposed Gaussian-Copula-BDM framework provides a theoretically sound and computationally efficient tool for dynamic safety control during arch bridge construction, enabling proactive risk management through continuous updating with monitoring data.

papers.title: Predictive modeling of homogenized mechanical properties for multifunctional gyroid-based aerospace structures
papers.abstract: Gyroid sheet networks are a promising core structure for multifunctional sandwich panels, offering excellent load-bearing capabilities alongside omnidirectional permeability. The key to exploiting their full lightweight potential is to predict the homogenized mechanical properties based on readily available solid material parameters. This study develops material-independent predictive models for the homogenized compressive modulus, yield strength, and strength by separating the Gyroid’s structural response from the contribution of the base material. Numerical and experimental investigations were carried out on Ti6Al4V and Nylon 11 at relative densities between 10 % and 60 % . Additional solid specimens form the basis for the material models and for normalizing the homogenized Gyroid properties. The results validate the material-independent modeling for the homogenized compressive modulus and yield strength across the entire investigated relative density range. The analysis of the homogenized compressive strength in combination with plastic strain distributions at the cellular level highlights the influence of base material strain hardening and ductility. Compared to the FE benchmark, practical imperfections reduce the experimentally measured homogenized mechanical properties by 15 % to 35 % . From an application perspective, the findings of this study establish a framework for designing load-bearing Gyroid cores for compressive stiffness and strength, independent of the specific base material.

papers.title: Primary and Secondary Stability of Subcrestal Morse-Taper Implants Placed Immediately into Extraction Sockets or into Grafted or Healed Ridges: A Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Immediate implant placement into fresh extraction sockets is often assumed to provide lower primary stability than placement into healed ridges, but comparative data for subcrestal Morse-taper (conical-connection) implants are lacking. This study compared insertion torque value (ITV) and implant stability quotient (ISQ) between two management protocols: immediate placement and delayed placement. Methods: This retrospective single-surgeon cohort included consecutive Argon K3 Pro implants placed in 2019–2022, grouped as immediate (IM), delayed into sites grafted within the preceding 12 months (DG) or delayed into healed ridges (HR). The protocols differed in more than timing (placement depth, grafting, flap design and healing management). ITV, ISQ at placement and ISQ at 3 months were compared with mixed-effects models accounting for multiple implants per patient. ISQ differences were tested against a post hoc ±5-unit equivalence margin; no equivalence test was applied to ITV. Results: Of 178 implants screened, 130 implants in 85 patients (52 women, 33 men) were analyzed: 56 IM, 30 DG and 44 HR. No difference was detected in ITV (delayed minus IM −1.4 Ncm, 95% CI −5.0 to 2.1), placement ISQ (IM 72.3 ± 7.8 vs. delayed 72.5 ± 9.0) or 3-month ISQ (78.8 ± 4.8 vs. 79.4 ± 5.6); in the primary analysis, the 90% confidence intervals of both ISQ differences lay within ±5 units, but the placement ISQ interval did not lie within ±3 units, and equivalence at placement was borderline in a size-adjusted sensitivity analysis. ISQ change was strongly related to starting ISQ (Spearman’s ρ = −0.77), largely through arithmetic coupling and regression to the mean, and baseline-adjusted 3-month ISQ did not differ between protocols (p = 0.46). All 19 immediate implants starting below ISQ 70 reached ISQ ≥ 70 by 3 months under the protocol used. In an exploratory analysis, ITV correlated with placement ISQ in healed ridges (ρ = 0.55) and more weakly in extraction sockets (ρ = 0.25); the difference between these correlations was inconsistent across methods. Conclusions: In this cohort, immediate and delayed protocols showed no detectable difference in insertion torque or ISQ, and ISQ differences were statistically within a post hoc ±5-unit margin. Whether torque is a weaker indicator of stability in extraction sockets is a hypothesis for prospective study.

papers.title: Model Predictive Control for Magnetically Actuated Cellbots
papers.abstract: This article presents a control strategy for, which are magnetically actuated, micron‐scale robots embedded into living cells. Our approach combines model predictive control, which provides low computational complexity and adaptability to changing environments, with Gaussian Processes (GPs), which are used as disturbance estimators for precise path tracking. To address the challenges posed by unmodeled dynamics, we integrate data‐driven modeling with model‐based control to accurately track desired trajectories using relatively small data. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to integrate data‐driven modeling with model‐based control for magnetically actuated cellbots. The GP effectively learns and predicts unmodeled disturbances, providing uncertainty bounds as well. The experimental results show that our controllers perform very well, even in environments cluttered with cells.

papers.title: Recent advances in multiscale modeling foundations for digital twins of hydrogen electrochemical devices
papers.abstract: Hydrogen energy plants, comprising of water electrolyzers, fuel cells, compressors, storage systems, and associated Balance of Plant components, represent a central pillar of the emerging green energy transition. Among the available hydrogen production pathways, green hydrogen produced via water electrolysis powered by renewable electricity is the most carbon-free route, and its efficient production and valorization through fuel cells necessitates a thorough understanding of the underlying electrochemical reactions and coupled physical processes. This mini-review summarizes fundamental process parameters, multiscale modeling strategies, and state-of-the-art digital twin integration frameworks across hydrogen production and utilization technologies. The interconnected physical phenomena of reaction reversibility, membrane ionic transport, catalyst and membrane degradation mechanisms, and heat and mass transfer are discussed as the essential governing equations that a faithful digital twin must encode. Furthermore, the multiscale modeling approaches applicable to these systems are reviewed across three hierarchical levels followed by discussion on cross-coupling and concepts of ROM/PINN integration along with CPS.

papers.title: Degradation-informed state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries using a Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network
papers.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries degrade during service through coupled electrochemical and thermal aging, causing capacity fade and increased operational risk. Accurate state-of-health (SOH) estimation is therefore required for battery health management. When only compact cycle-level descriptors are available, maintaining prediction accuracy together with model interpretability remains difficult. This study proposes a degradation-informed hyperparameter-optimized Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (HPO-TabPFN) framework for SOH estimation. Each cycle is represented using temporal, energy-related and incremental-capacity descriptors, chronological context is constructed for TabPFN, and inference-related hyperparameters are optimized. Grid search, random search, particle swarm optimization and Bayesian optimization (BO) are evaluated under the same temporal validation protocol. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) is used to analyze local feature attribution, and Sobol analysis is used to quantify model-output sensitivity and interaction effects. On the evaluated NASA and CALCE cell sequences, hyperparameter optimization reduced the prediction error of TabPFN, and the Bayesian-optimized model achieved average mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) values of 0.2450% and 0.1800%, respectively. Under the same chronological delayed-label protocol, BO-TabPFN gave the lowest error among the unoptimized TabPFN and the evaluated baseline regressors on the tested cells. These results indicate that cycling-derived health indicators can support accurate tabular SOH estimation in the evaluated public datasets, while the NASA B05 case study illustrates how the fitted estimator depends on the selected health factors under the stated attribution and sensitivity settings.

papers.title: Degradation-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Battery Energy Storage Dispatch in Industrial Microgrids and Its Real-Time Deployment Validation
papers.abstract: Battery degradation is a non-negligible cost in battery energy storage (BESS) dispatch for industrial microgrids, yet most deep reinforcement learning (DRL) studies optimize only the procurement cost. This paper embeds a rainflow-calibrated cyclic aging cost into the reward of a degradation-aware soft actor-critic (DA-SAC) framework with an adjustable weight λ, making the cost–lifetime trade-off explicit. On one year of 15 min data from an industrial microgrid in Chongqing, the main evaluation is conducted in an offline simulation, and the typical days are validated by hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) real-time simulation on the Speedgoat real-time target with the policy on a Beckhoff edge controller. DA-SAC reduces the cyclic degradation cost by about 28% relative to MPC, but its operating cost cannot go below CNY 649.4/day, worse than a simple price threshold rule (641.8), a boundary we attribute to long-horizon credit assignment. Dynamic programming (DP) provides a strong baseline whose closed-loop lookup reaches cost parity with MPC under noisy forecasts (CNY 618.4 vs. 618.1/day), and deployment time SAC correction improves the coarse-grid DP from CNY 620.6 to 619.4/day, with greater forecast noise robustness (+3.5% vs. +4.55% for MPC under a three-fold noise increase). Degradation-aware DRL is therefore most valuable when combined with the exact opportunity cost of DP under a single main site and a fixed forecast noise level.

papers.title: Two-stage fundamental Bayesian model updating method based on MCMC algorithm
papers.abstract: Model updating plays an important role in obtaining a more accurate finite element model (FEM) based on measured vibration data. Based on the updated FEM, it is more convenient to carry out further analysis, e.g., structural health monitoring, digital twin, and so on. Bayesian model updating methods are attracting more attention since they can provide rigorous models and evaluate the uncertainty of the updated results. However, in the real application, it still has some problems such as computational efficiency and accuracy. In this paper, a two-stage Bayesian function combined with MCMC algorithm is proposed and used to perform model updating of a real complicated long-span cable-stayed bridge. The two-stage Bayesian function can automatically consider the heteroscedasticity of each utilized modal degree and it allows for incomplete modal information for model updating. Before conducting model updating, two different sensitivity analysis functions are used for local and global sensitivity analysis of bridge model. A set of interaction process between different computation tools has been established to improve computational speed by using an improved stopping criterion. The updated results are demonstrated for both model classes, and ultimately a Bayesian model class evidence was used to judge their superiority. The proposed method was verified by a numerical example and then applied in the updating of the bridge. The experimental results show that the model updating method successfully corrects initial FEMs with reverse mode order errors using incomplete modal information. Simultaneously, the results exhibit a relatively low level of uncertainty. Furthermore, the Bayesian model class selection algorithm proves that new sensitivity analysis functions are superior.

papers.title: Tribological and Microstructural Characterization of LPBF-Fabricated AlSi10Mg Composites with B₄C Reinforcement
papers.abstract: In this investigation, AlSi10Mg matrix composites reinforced with varying boron carbide (B4C) content (0–3 wt.%)were fabricated using the LPBF process. The SEM analysis of raw powders confirmed spherical AlSi10Mg particles and angular B4C particles. Microstructural examination of the fabricated specimens revealed a fine cellular α-Al matrix with a continuous Si-rich eutectic network. Hardness increased progressively with B4C addition, rising from approximately 132–204 HV. Owing to reinforcement of B4C reinforcement an improvement in hardness was nearly 54%. Tribological studies showed a significant reduction in wear loss, which decreased from around 2.512 mg for 0 wt.% B4C to nearly 0.715 mg for 3 wt.% B4C.SEM analysis of worn surfaces demonstrated a transition from severe adhesive and oxidative wear in monolithic AlSi10Mg to mild abrasive and delamination-controlled wear. The enhanced hardness, reduced wear loss, and stable frictional behavior confirm the effectiveness of B4C reinforcement in improving the tribological performance.

papers.title: The successor representation in high-risk drinking and alcohol-related contexts
papers.abstract: The successor representation (SR) is a reinforcement learning strategy which has been suggested to underlie nuanced forms of habitual behavior, rendering it a candidate mechanism for mental health conditions thought to involve habitual control, such as addiction. However, paradigms used to assess habits in humans cannot detect SR use. Together with the fact that they are usually conducted in disorder-irrelevant contexts, this may explain why the evidence for a hypothesized shift from goal-directed to habitual behavior in addiction is inconsistent. Here, we tested whether individuals with high-risk ( n = 260) compared to low-risk drinking behavior ( n = 260) rely more on SR or a rigid goal-based dimension-reduced SR variant, particularly in alcohol-related contexts. An online multi-stage decision-making task performed in either a virtual bar or apartment context allowed us to dissociate (red)SR from model-based and model-free learning strategies by testing how well participants adapted their choices to different types of distal changes in the environment. Findings suggest that a particular type of SR, namely a (reduced) random-policy SR-like strategy, contributes to human behavior, but that high-risk drinkers do not differ from low-risk drinkers in their use of this strategy. Instead, both groups seem to rely less on what is likely a (reduced) random-policy SR strategy in alcohol-related contexts – and instead more on model-free control. Results suggest that the use of an adaptive, resource-efficient decision-making strategy is selectively downregulated in substance-related contexts. This study highlights the importance of considering contextual modulation and nuanced decision strategies in understanding habitual and goal-directed behavior in mental health conditions such as addiction.

papers.title: A PINN-assisted physics-guided meta-heuristic optimization method for material–energy synergy in converter steelmaking
papers.abstract: Converter steelmaking simultaneously consumes metallic inputs and utility energy, generates recoverable BOFG and steam, and must satisfy strict endpoint-quality constraints. Existing optimization studies generally treat material utilization, energy consumption, and process quality separately, which cannot fully represent their coupled effects. This study develops a mechanism–data hybrid and physics-guided optimization framework for material–energy synergy in converter steelmaking. A synergy-degree model is established using material-flow and energy-flow order parameters. A multi-output physics-informed neural network surrogate is developed to predict BOFG, steam, endpoint carbon content, and endpoint temperature, with a thermodynamic recovery constraint incorporated into the loss function. The resulting constrained nonlinear problem is solved using the physics-guided dynamic Harris hawks optimizer (PGDHHO), which combines Tent chaotic initialization, nonlinear escape-energy scheduling, and penalty-triggered Lévy-flight repair. Using 600 industrial charges, the PINN achieves R² values of 0.972, 0.969, 0.967, and 0.961 for BOFG, steam, endpoint temperature, and endpoint carbon content, respectively. For ten test-set charges, the mean charge-level synergy improvement is 23.75%, while the mean synergy degree increases from 0.4903 to 0.6056. The average net energy consumption changes from −19.310 to −20.857 kgce/t steel, and the mean furnace-level carbon-emission reduction reaches 19.27%. In 30 independent algorithm runs, the proposed method achieves a mean fitness of 0.594 and a standard deviation of 0.004. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves material–energy coordination while reducing net energy consumption and carbon emissions under endpoint-quality constraints.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction Sets for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Disease Diagnosis Under Co-Occurring Crop Symptoms: A Computer Set-Validity Evaluation
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction has been proposed as a distribution-free method for quantifying uncertainty in artificial intelligence (AI) crop-disease classifiers, yet its validity guarantees assume exchangeability between calibration and test data. When multiple diseases co-occur on the same plant, the label space becomes set-valued and the exchangeability assumption is strained in ways that existing evaluations do not address. The framework distinguishes marginal from conditional coverage, defines a co-occurrence-adjusted nonconformity score, and derives bounds on the coverage gap induced by symptom overlap. A replication-based evaluation was conducted using a before-after-control-impact design with a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64). Power was estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power. The results show that set-validity degrades systematically as co-occurrence prevalence increases, and that the degradation is not captured by marginal coverage diagnostics. Conditional coverage diagnostics are necessary for responsible deployment of conformal prediction in agricultural disease diagnosis.

papers.title: Bayesian modelling of salinity profiles in the Volturno River mouth under depth dependence
papers.abstract: Abstract Saltwater intrusion is a recurrent environmental hazard for Mediterranean coastal systems, and identifying which physico-chemical variables track salinity is central to monitoring design. Estimating such associations from depth-resolved profiles requires two features of the data to be addressed: the uncertainty of each depth-bin summary, arising from pooling readings taken at several stations along a steep longitudinal gradient, and the residual vertical dependence left after conditioning on the covariates. This paper proposes a Bayesian errors-in-variables-like model with a Gaussian process component for residual depth structure, applied to two synoptic campaigns in the Volturno River mouth (Italy) under contrasting winter and summer hydrological conditions. The results show that temperature is consistently associated with salinity, but the sign of the association differs between the two seasonal conditions during sampling: it is positive in winter and negative in summer within the reach occupied by the salt wedge. Dissolved oxygen is important in winter only. The residual depth amplitude is small in both campaigns, while the complementary full river reach analysis for the summer campaign yields a substantially larger residual depth component, showing that the fitted relationship is sensitive to the sampled river reach. Under near-perfect collinearity the ordering of the covariates is better identified than any individual coefficient, and is reported through posterior rank probabilities. A simulation study shows that the specification maintains nominal credible-interval coverage where a naive regression collapses to a few per cent and reverses a tracer coefficient’s sign in up to 45 per cent of replicates. Cross-validation on held-out depth bins supports predictive adequacy within each campaign, while over comparable river reaches the estimated relationships are specific to the contrasting hydrological regimes represented by the two campaigns and do not transfer between them.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Based Modeling and Optimization of Continuous Biomanufacturing Processes: A Data-Driven Simulation Study
papers.abstract: Continuous biomanufacturing, particularly perfusion-based monoclonal-antibody production, offers highproductivity and consistent quality but requires faster, more reliable monitoring and control thanconventional fed-batch operation. This paper reviews digital-twin-based optimisation of continuousbiomanufacturing and presents an illustrative, reproducible simulation informed by publicly availablebioprocess datasets. A three-tier digital-model, digital-shadow, and digital-twin architecture is examinedalongside mechanistic, data-driven, and hybrid modelling paradigms. The simulation demonstrates modelpredictive control of glucose set-point tracking in a perfusion bioreactor. Across the reviewed studies andillustrative results, hybrid mechanistic-machine-learning twins provide stronger predictive performancethan purely mechanistic or data-driven alternatives, while digital-twin-based control reduces glucosedeviation relative to conventional control and open-loop feeding. Key barriers include fragmenteddatasets, model validation, regulatory acceptance, cybersecurity, and cross-scale transferability. The studytherefore recommends open, standardised bioprocess datasets and rigorous deployment validation tosupport reproducible, industrially credible digital-twin research.

papers.title: Knowledge-guided hierarchical deep learning for large-space fire temperature-field reconstruction
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a hierarchical collaborative deep learning framework to address physical inconsistency and the reliability bottleneck induced by parameter uncertainty in large-space fire temperature field reconstruction. The framework integrates state identification, physical-parameter inference, and spatial reconstruction. First, a cascaded temporal feature extraction module using LSTM-FS identifies fire combustion stages. Then, a specialized LSTM-BiEC model autonomously predicts fire source coordinates and physical constants from discrete sensor time series, effectively mitigating epistemic uncertainty associated with manual parameter presetting. Finally, a physics-informed neural network based on the bi-exponential radial diffusion law (RCDBiE-PINN) reconstructs high-fidelity steady-state temperature fields. Compared to existing single-exponential decay or data-only models, this framework more accurately captures near-source extreme values and far-field decay characteristics. This study’s main contribution lies in its ability to automatically represent, infer, and utilize fire dynamics knowledge from sparse sensor data. By converting raw sensor streams into explicit fire-state and physical-parameter knowledge and using this knowledge to instantiate a physics-constrained reconstruction model, the framework reduces repeated manual state identification and parameter presetting during scene-level deployment and provides a machine-readable temperature-field interface for downstream safety assessment.

papers.title: A Physics-Guided Adaptive Bayesian Optimization Framework for Training-Free Underwater Image Enhancement
papers.abstract: Reliable underwater visual perception plays a critical role in marine exploration, autonomous underwater vehicles, and subsea inspection. Nevertheless, underwater images are frequently degraded by severe color distortion, contrast reduction, and structural information loss due to wavelength-dependent light attenuation and scattering. Existing enhancement approaches either depend on fixed physical assumptions or require data-driven models, which often limits their adaptability across diverse underwater environments. To address these challenges, this paper presents a Physics-Guided Adaptive Bayesian Optimization (PG-ABO) framework for training-free underwater image enhancement. By combining physical degradation priors with image-specific parameter optimization, the proposed approach enables enhancement strategies to adapt dynamically to varying underwater conditions without relying on paired training data. The proposed framework incorporates an improved underwater dark channel prior with structure-aware transmission refinement to establish a physically consistent initial representation. Subsequently, a dual-path optimization strategy is constructed to generate complementary enhancement candidates by separately targeting color fidelity and structural perception. Bayesian optimization is employed to adaptively search enhancement parameters under the guidance of UCIQE and UIQM objectives. Furthermore, a robust multi-scale fusion strategy with anti-hotspot weight regulation is introduced, while a metric-aware refinement module is applied to enhance perceptual consistency and reduce enhancement artifacts. Experiments conducted on three underwater image datasets, including U45, UIEB, and LSUI, verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework across diverse underwater conditions. Consequently, the proposed method provides an adaptive, training-free, and physically motivated solution for underwater image enhancement under complex degradation conditions.

papers.title: Inkjet and Related Printing Technologies for Plant Systems: From Physiological Monitoring to Functional Biofabrication
papers.abstract: Featuring non-contact, high-precision, and multi-material deposition, inkjet and related printing technologies offer a new alternative technique for plant systems. However, the spatial heterogeneity, continuous growth, and sensitivity of plant tissues to external perturbations make it difficult for conventional methods to target specific sites on living organs. This review evaluates thermal and piezoelectric inkjet printing, together with aerosol jet and electrohydrodynamic printing for plant applications. Moreover, it relates the jetting behavior of the printhead to interfacial processes between droplets and plant surfaces. Practical performance is assessed across four dimensions: effective feature size, organ-scale throughput, potential biological damage, and the physiological compatibility of printing inks with plants. Applications are then organized within a framework comprising five tiers: monitoring, delivery, sensing, biofabrication, and intelligent systems. Specifically, recent studies have demonstrated that these printing approaches can be employed for surface labeling and growth tracking of plant organs, localized delivery of agricultural inputs, fabrication of flexible sensors, and construction of living materials (e.g., plant cells). Combined with artificial intelligence technology, these capabilities could form a closed-loop system spanning sensing to feedback, with printing as the precision actuator, potentially shifting plant management from passive observation to active regulation. Finally, this review discusses the challenges of living-interface dynamics, ink biocompatibility, multiscale integration, and data intelligence. It further outlines the prospects of these technologies for programmable plants and living agricultural interfaces. By bridging printing technologies, plant systems, and functional biofabrication, this review provides a unified framework to guide the development of intelligent and sustainable agricultural systems.

papers.abstract: The use of internet-based technologies has driven the adoption of active learning strategies in higher education. Among these, the flipped classroom has been widely studied, though empirical evidence regarding its application in university contexts within the Peruvian highlands remains limited. The objective of this study was to analyze the impact of a flipped classroom strategy on the development of research skills among students enrolled in a thesis proposal course at a public university in southern Peru. This study employed a quantitative approach with an explanatory scope and a pre-experimental pretest–posttest design. Nineteen students participated in the pretest, and twenty-three participated in the posttest. Results indicate an average increase of 4.18 points in research skills following the intervention. papers.title: Application of a Capacitive Sensor with a ZrO2 Thin Coating and Artificial Intelligence to Determine the Amount of Diesel in Water
papers.abstract: Reliable determination of diesel contamination in water remains challenging due to the heterogeneous nature of diesel–water dispersions and the frequency-dependent dielectric response of multiphase systems. This study investigates the performance of capacitive sensors with ZrO2 coatings of 2, 4, and 6 μm thickness and proposes a physics-informed computational framework for predicting sensor response and estimating diesel content in water. Experimental capacitance measurements were performed at 13 frequencies ranging from 10 Hz to 300 kHz using diesel–water mixtures with different fuel contents. The results revealed a general decrease in capacitance with increasing diesel content and measurement frequency, with the most pronounced concentration-dependent differences observed in the 102–104 Hz range. The 2 μm coating exhibited the highest sensitivity to diesel content, whereas the 6 μm coating provided improved measurement stability and the highest calibration linearity (R2 = 0.733) at an operating frequency of 10 kHz. To support sensor interpretation, a six-dimensional process–structure–property (PSP) model was developed to simulate the relationships between ZrO2 deposition conditions, coating microstructure, and functional properties. In parallel, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) incorporating monotonicity and high-frequency stabilization constraints was implemented for forward capacitance prediction and inverse diesel content estimation. The PINN achieved a mean absolute error of 0.29 mL in the reported inverse estimation evaluation, demonstrating the potential of physics-informed learning for interpreting nonlinear sensor responses. The complementary PSP and PINN modules establish a preliminary framework for future digital twin development, although direct numerical coupling between them remains to be implemented. The results demonstrate the feasibility of combining ZrO2-coated capacitive sensing with physics-informed artificial intelligence and provide a foundation for further development of virtual sensors for diesel–water monitoring applications.

papers.title: The future of three-dimensional printing in healthcare: A competitive technology intelligence-based scientometric and patent landscape of three-dimensional bioprinting
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) printing is increasingly transforming healthcare through advances in materials and manufacturing processes, along with the growing demand for personalized therapeutic solutions. Although substantial research has focused on materials, fabrication processes, and specific biomedical applications, comparatively less attention has been devoted to systematically integrating scientific and patent evidence to identify technological trends, innovation trajectories, and emerging opportunities. In this context, competitive technology intelligence (CTI) provides a systematic framework for integrating scientific and patent information to examine technological evolution and support the identification of emerging trajectories and opportunities. This study applied the CTI methodology to quantitatively characterize the scientific and technological landscape of 3D bioprinting and tissue engineering, while fiber-based fabrication and 3D-printed oral drug delivery were incorporated as contextual domains based on published evidence. Scientific publications and patent families published between 2021 and 2025 on 3D bioprinting and tissue engineering were analyzed using Web of Science and The Lens platform. The final datasets comprised 6,916 scientific publications and 732 simple patent families. Annual scientific publication output increased from 1,061 records in 2021 to 1,705 in 2025 (+60.7%), while published simple patent families increased from 98 to 193 (+96.9%), with year-to-year variation. China and the United States showed the highest scientific publication output. The leading patent-family jurisdictions and filing routes represented in the dataset were the World Intellectual Property Organization (380 families), the United States (363), China (306), and the European Patent Office (219); these counts were non-exclusive. The most frequently represented International Patent Classification classes were B33Y10/00 (235 patent families), B33Y80/00 (234), and A61L27/52 (210). The results revealed an expansion of scientific and inventive activity, while their integration with published evidence highlighted persistent challenges in reproducibility, biological validation, scale-up, regulation, and clinical translation. Overall, this CTI-based landscape contributes to the identification of the scientific and technological trajectories in 3D bioprinting and tissue engineering, while situating them within the broader healthcare 3D printing context, and provides strategic insights to support research prioritization, innovation planning, and future translational efforts.

papers.title: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control-Based Reverse Path-Planning and Path-Tracking Control of a Vehicle with Trailer System
papers.abstract: Reverse parking of a vehicle with a trailer is a challenging task to complete for human drivers due to its articulated structure, unstable reverse-motion behaviors, and unintuitive steering responses. This paper proposes a compact, trailer-centric nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC)-based automation routine that integrates local motion generation and feedback control into a single receding-horizon framework, without requiring a separately planned reference path or a dedicated path-tracking controller. The trailer unit is represented as a virtual standalone vehicle, and its motion requirements are mapped to the vehicle unit inputs via inverse kinematics. This allows the trajectory prediction and tracking objective to be represented only with trailer states, hence reducing the dimensions of the horizon-stacked state and weighting matrices compared to using the full vehicle-trailer formulation. The proposed controller is implemented as a single-shooting nonlinear program (NLP) and supports a three-stage maneuver sequence to obtain an improved final parking configuration. Simulation results demonstrate successful vehicle-trailer parking maneuvers, while hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) results further illustrate that online NMPC computation times can remain within the real-time sampling deadline, indicating that the proposed NMPC framework can offer a practical receding-horizon automation routine for vehicle-trailer reverse parking tasks.

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for the Thermal–Hydraulic Modeling of Normal Operation in Superconducting Coils for Fusion Applications
papers.abstract: Transient conjugate heat transfer in coupled solid–fluid systems is governed by diffusion, advection, and heat transfer processes that can make repeated simulations expensive and time-consuming in the design phase. This study develops a physics-informed neural network for one-dimensional coupled solid–fluid heat transfer. The model takes space, time, and operating parameters as inputs and predicts the temperature fields in both the solid and fluid domains. The governing equations, heat transfer, boundary conditions, and initial conditions are incorporated into the training through differentiable residual losses, reducing the reliance on high-fidelity training data. The proposed approach is formulated in nondimensional form and evaluated using metrics that quantify conservation, boundary conditions satisfaction, and prediction accuracy. Particular attention is paid to the model behavior within the training range and when operating conditions extend beyond it. The resulting framework provides a basis for the thermal–hydraulic assessment of the performance of superconducting coils for fusion applications in different operating scenarios under evaluation during the design optimization phase using the physics-informed neural network approach. The analyzed case study is the Central Solenoid of the DTT facility currently under construction at ENEA Frascati in Italy.

papers.title: An interpretable DM-PINN for retrieving mangrove canopy carbon, nitrogen, and potassium contents using Sentinel-2 and SDGSAT-1 observations along China's southeastern coast
papers.abstract: Mangroves are among the most important blue carbon ecosystems, contributing substantially to global carbon sequestration and biodiversity conservation. Canopy carbon (CCC), nitrogen (CNC), and potassium (CKC) contents provide critical indicators of nutrient cycling, ecosystem functioning, and ecological health. However, the structural complexity and strong spatial heterogeneity of mangroves present major obstacles to understanding the spectral response mechanisms and achieving reliable large-scale retrieval of these biochemical parameters. To address these limitations, we developed an interpretable retrieval framework that integrates causal analysis with physical constraints for reliable estimation of mangrove biochemical parameters. First, we proposed a Multi-Channel Chatterjee-Enhanced Correlation Spectrum Analysis (MC-ξ-CS) method that integrates causal discovery to systematically identify spectral bands causally associated with CCC, CNC, and CKC. For large-scale retrieval of mangrove canopy parameters, the identified causal relationships were transferred to satellite observations through a Global Angle-Divergence Spectral Transfer (GADT) framework, yielding robust estimation (R2 = 0.511–0.669). Subsequently, a Dual-Mechanism Guided Physics-Informed Neural Network (DM-PINN) was developed to synergistically integrate causal analysis and physical constraints, achieving robust retrieval performance (R2 = 0.604–0.83) for three representative mangrove species and enhancing the physical interpretability of the results. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first comprehensive large-scale retrieval of key mangrove biochemical parameters along the southeastern coast of China, revealing CCC values of 409.18–566.89 g/kg (C/N = 9.77–14.21), CNC values of 14.38–74.9 g/kg (N/K = 1.99–3.86), and CKC values of 4.78–19.67 g/kg (C/K = 28.22–37.67). Distinct inter-provincial spatial patterns were observed: CNC and CKC exhibited similar gradients, increasing from landward to seaward regions, whereas CCC displayed an opposite spatial distribution pattern with lower values in coastal regions. Moreover, CCC was strongly positively correlated with CNC, while CKC showed negative correlations with both parameters. Collectively, this study established a novel theoretical and methodological framework for elucidating the spectral response mechanisms of mangrove biochemical parameters, offering critical scientific support for large-scale mangrove degradation monitoring, ecological restoration assessment, and biodiversity conservation.

summary_zh.method: 结合因果谱分析与物理约束，构建双机制引导的DM-PINN反演碳氮钾含量。
summary_zh.result: 三类红树物种反演R2达0.604–0.83，并揭示省际空间分布格局。
summary_zh.validation: 基于Sentinel-2与SDGSAT-1卫星观测的遥感反演精度评估。

summary_en.motivation: The structural complexity and spatial heterogeneity of mangroves hinder reliable large-scale retrieval of canopy biochemical parameters from spectral data.
summary_en.method: A causal spectral analysis identifies causally relevant bands, which are transferred to satellite observations and fused into a dual-mechanism physics-informed neural network for retrieval.
summary_en.result: The framework attains R2 of 0.604–0.83 across three mangrove species and reveals distinct inter-provincial spatial gradients in carbon, nitrogen, and potassium contents.
summary_en.validation: Retrieval accuracy is assessed against field-referenced biochemical measurements using Sentinel-2 and SDGSAT-1 satellite observations.

papers.title: Research on the Application of Ensemble Learning Model in Cavity Noise Spectrum Prediction
papers.abstract: Rapid prediction of cavity sound pressure spectra is essential for the acoustic design of high-speed vehicles. A spectral database is built from 20 flow conditions (4 Mach numbers × 5 angles of attack) and eight cavity measurement points, giving 160 condition–point combinations, each densely sampled at 1147 amplitude–frequency points over 6–7000 Hz. Four models—RF, XGBoost, LightGBM and SVM—are compared on two prediction tasks, flow-condition and spatial-position prediction, before and after Bayesian optimization. Optimization markedly improves in-distribution accuracy and reduces dominant-frequency amplitude errors under unseen conditions, but reverses the ranking: RF and LightGBM dominate at baseline, whereas XGBoost ranks first after tuning, attaining 0.76 dB in the flow-condition task and staying on a par with RF (0.09 dB apart) in the spatial-position task. Under unseen conditions the SVM degenerates to a constant output of 117.11 dB, essentially the training-target mean, owing to the locality of the RBF kernel—a structural limitation that tuning cannot remedy. The direction of the peak-amplitude bias is not uniform: systematic underestimation occurs in the spatial-position task, whereas after tuning XGBoost overestimates the peak at Ma = 1.5, the condition with the highest measured amplitude. No single model is optimal across all scenarios.

papers.title: PENERAPAN MODUL PEMBELAJARAN BERBASIS PROYEK DAN ACTIVE LEARNING PADA ENGLISH FOR OPTOMETRY DI ARO GAPOPIN
papers.abstract: English proficiency has become an essential competency for optometry students, particularly for understanding scientific literature, communicating with international patients, and enhancing professional readiness in the global era. However, English learning in the optometry field still encounters challenges, such as limited student engagement and the lack of contextual learning resources. This study aims to describe the implementation of project-based learning modules combined with active learning strategies in the English for Optometry course at ARO Gapopin. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, with data collected through observation, interviews, and documentation. The results indicate that the use of project-based modules encouraged students to engage more actively in the learning process through practical assignments, including optometry case presentations, clinical service simulations, and the creation of academic products in English. The integration of active learning strategies was found to enhance students’ motivation, collaboration, and reflective learning skills. It is concluded that project-based modules combined with active learning effectively improved English for Optometry instruction, particularly in mastering professional terminology and applying it in real-life contexts. Future research is recommended to employ a quantitative or mixed methods approach to measure the effectiveness of this model more comprehensively, as well as to explore its impact on students’ professional communication skills in the long term.

papers.title: Dynamic thermal imaging for crop water stress detection across phenological stages: Enhancing irrigation scheduling precision
papers.abstract: Thermal remote sensing and derived indices such as the crop water stress index (CWSI) can assess crop water status and support precision irrigation. However, most operational and artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches rely on fixed, season-long thresholds to interpret canopy–air temperature differences and often overlook the influence of crop phenology. This review synthesises evidence from grapevine, wheat, maize, potato and several other crops on how developmental stage affects the non-water-stressed baseline (NWSB), CWSI thresholds and irrigation-scheduling algorithms. It covers CWSI theory and estimation practices; crop-specific, phenology-dependent behaviour of baselines and thresholds; a comparison of threshold-based, machine learning, Internet of Things (IoT), digital twin and Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)-56 approaches with respect to crop phenology; and a conceptual framework for phenology-aware scheduling. Across the reviewed crops, baseline behaviour generally varied systematically across the growing season, the relationship between CWSI and crop water status generally strengthened after canopy closure and CWSI measured during reproductive stages was generally most closely related to yield. A quantitative audit of 56 AI-, thermal-imaging-, or CWSI-based studies found that 78.6 % either did not explicitly incorporate crop phenology or relied on day of year as a temporal proxy, whereas only 5.4 % explicitly encoded phenological stage. The proposed framework considers phenology explicitly in baseline estimation, threshold setting and data fusion or machine learning for irrigation scheduling; the framework will require multi-year, multi-site field validation before operational use. Future research should prioritise standardised phenology definitions and long-term, multi-location studies to establish and validate stage-specific parameters.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Predictive Maintenance of Mission-Critical Engineered Systems: A Systematic Review of Methods, Frameworks, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Asset management in safety-critical industries is moving away from calendar-driven preventive schedules and toward autonomous, data-driven decision-making enabled by artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML). This work reports a PRISMA-compliant systematic review of the predictive maintenance (PdM) literature published between January 2018 and June 2026, covering domains such as aerospace, energy, and advanced manufacturing where component degradation must be tracked with high reliability. A structured search across four bibliographic databases (IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Web of Science, and the ACM Digital Library) produced an initial pool of 2,847 candidate records; after multi-stage screening, 127 peer-reviewed studies were retained for detailed synthesis. The retained literature is organized into six methodological threads: purely data-driven learning, physics-informed machine learning, digital-twin architectures, causal and explainable AI, uncertainty quantification, and human-AI collaboration. Although deep architectures achieve strong benchmark accuracy, the synthesis surfaces recurring shortcomings around out-of-distribution robustness, epistemic uncertainty handling, and model opacity. Eight recurring research gaps are catalogued, and a forward-looking agenda is proposed, culminating in a conceptual unifying framework, referred to here as NEXUS-AI, that combines physical priors, neuro-symbolic reasoning, and human oversight to support verifiable reliability in high-consequence settings.

papers.title: Economic Evaluation of Unconventional Tight Oil Resource
papers.abstract: The Wolfcamp field, a significant tight oil play in the Permian Basin, exhibits a matrix permeability of approximately 0.0005 mD. In this research, hydraulic fracturing modelling and simulation was conducted on a targeted area of this field using PROSPER (Production System Performance) and CMG (Computer Modelling Group) software, resulting in a permeability improvement to 1.57 mD. This enhancement contributed to an improvement of the oil recovery factor by approximately 2.2% and of the gas recovery factor by about 10%, significantly boosting production potential. A detailed economic evaluation was performed using key financial metrics. The net present value (NPV) was found to be approximately $26 million, a strong indicator of profitability. Furthermore, the internal rate of return (IRR) was calculated to be approximately 34%, which is well above typical industry hurdle rates. The payback period of 2 years, 9 months and 14 days further supports the feasibility of the project by indicating a relatively quick capital recovery. A short payback period is particularly beneficial in the volatile oil and gas market, reducing financial risk and improving cash flow stability. Unconventional oil development is highly uncertain; to address these uncertainties, an advanced stochastic economic analysis was performed using Python, which allowed a more comprehensive evaluation than traditional tools such as Excel. Unlike conventional methods, Python enables simultaneous multivariable interaction, capturing the complex relationships between key economic parameters and project outcomes. This study demonstrated that Python-based stochastic modelling provides a 10% improvement in uncertainty quantification compared with the conventional Excel spreadsheet, enhancing decision-making accuracy. Therefore, to enhance production and ensure investment reliability in tight oil developments, integration of stochastic economic analysis is necessary.

papers.title: Stochastic model predictive control for PV–BESS microgrid energy management under demand charge
papers.abstract: Behind-the-meter microgrid energy management faces a temporal discrepancy: 15 min control decisions must account for financial penalties consolidated over 30-day billing cycles. Under hybrid tariffs combining time-of-use charges with monthly peak demand penalties, costs are assessed against the highest 15 min average power within the billing month, exposing short-horizon controllers to avoidable penalties. Existing stochastic and robust Model Predictive Control (MPC) formulations treat demand billing as a static constraint, without adapting to the cycle’s accumulated exposure. This paper closes that gap with a Stochastic MPC (SMPC) architecture integrating a discrete historical peak state variable into a receding-horizon Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation that minimizes total operating cost, comprising energy procurement, demand/generation billing penalties net of the historical peak, degradation, and smoothing terms, over the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) charge/discharge trajectory. Control is restricted to BESS dispatch, excluding load shedding and solar curtailment. Load and photovoltaic forecast uncertainty is quantified via a hybrid probabilistic framework combining a conformal-prediction-calibrated XGBoost load model with a four-model numerical weather prediction ensemble for solar, with real-time mismatches mitigated through asymmetric bias correction and adaptive scenario reweighting. Validated on a medium-voltage university campus microgrid, the SMPC achieves a 12.57% cost reduction relative to an uncontrolled baseline (no energy storage). Two ablations isolate this gain’s sources: a Perfect Foresight MPC attributes only 1.21% to load forecasting uncertainty, while a deterministic MPC retaining the same billing-memory architecture but without scenario-based treatment costs 11.75% more, identifying stochastic treatment, not billing memory alone, as the primary driver of savings.
